+<Form schema={schema} uiSchema={uiSchema} validator={validator} onChange={logChange} />;

@rjsf/mui's descriptions render a div rather than an <h6> BREAKING CHANGE​

This affects a style or a test that finds a field's description, or a selected option's, as an h6 or by the heading role. DescriptionField rendered each description as an <h6> heading, which listed every description among the form's headings. It now renders a div with the same look. To get the <h6> back, give the description's Typography a component, in a field's ui:options or for every field in ui:globalOptions (a field with its own ui:options.mui needs it there too):

 const uiSchema = {
   'ui:globalOptions': {
+    mui: { rjsfSlotProps: { descTypography: { component: 'h6' } } },
   },
 };

An object's or an array's group has role="group" and the field's id BREAKING CHANGE​

This affects a style or a test that finds a container's parts by where they sit in the DOM, by the group role, or by the field's id. An object's or an array's title, description and contents are now a group, named by the title and described by the field's errors, description and help, so a screen reader reads them together (#5723):

  • In @rjsf/chakra-ui, @rjsf/fluentui-rc, @rjsf/mui and @rjsf/react-bootstrap, ObjectFieldTemplate rendered them with no element around them, and in @rjsf/fluentui-rc so did ArrayFieldTemplate. They now render inside a div with role="group" carrying the field's id.
  • @rjsf/daisyui's ArrayFieldTemplate and ObjectFieldTemplate, @rjsf/mantine's ObjectFieldTemplate, and the ArrayFieldTemplate of @rjsf/chakra-ui, @rjsf/mui and @rjsf/react-bootstrap give the element they already rendered role="group", and the field's id where it didn't carry it.
  • A <fieldset>, which every other container renders, is a group already, and only gains the name and description.

Point a child selector at the new div, as in [role="group"] > .... A test calling getByRole('group') can now find the root object's group as well, so give it the group's name or search within the field:

-screen.getByRole('group');
+screen.getByRole('group', { name: 'Pets' });

AltDateWidget date parts are named in every theme BREAKING CHANGE​

Each select an AltDateWidget (and AltDateTimeWidget) renders is a control of its own: DateElement gives it the date part's id, such as root__year, as both its id and its name, and the name prop it used to take is ignored and deprecated. Each part is named by the field's label and the part, such as When, year, in every theme, @rjsf/mantine included, even when the field hides its label, so the parts of two date fields stay distinct; only a field with no label at all leaves the part alone, such as year (#5355). Each part is also described by the field's description, help and errors, which no part was linked to before. A test querying a part by its own name, or by the value it displays, no longer matches when the field has a label:

-screen.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'year' });
+screen.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'When, year' });

The parts' names and placeholders go through translateString as TranslatableString.YearLabel, MonthLabel, DayLabel, HourLabel, MinuteLabel and SecondLabel, and the way the field's label and the part are combined goes through TranslatableString.DateElementAriaLabel ('%1, %2'), so a locale can reorder them or change the separator (#5357). Their english defaults are the lowercase part names the widgets displayed before, so a form without a custom translateString displays the same text.

DateElement hands the name and the description to the registry's SelectWidget as its aria-label and aria-describedby, which every theme's SelectWidget now gives to the control a screen reader focuses through the new widgetAriaProps(), describing it by the caller's ids and, while it shows one, by the id of the selected option's description, the one element it renders itself, listed where it is drawn among the field's description and help. A replacement SelectWidget must do the same, or the date parts it renders are left unnamed and undescribed; no other widget is required to honor the two props:

import { widgetAriaProps } from '@rjsf/utils';

function MySelectWidget(props: WidgetProps) {
  return <select id={props.id} {...widgetAriaProps(props)}>{/* ... */}</select>;
}

Three theme changes follow from this. @rjsf/mui's SelectWidget describes its combobox rather than the field's root, and an aria-label or aria-describedby set in an htmlInput given through rjsfSlotProps still wins over both. @rjsf/fluentui-rc's SelectWidget no longer renders an empty <label> for a field with no label, which named the dropdown by nothing. @rjsf/shadcn's single SelectWidget trigger is a combobox, which holds the option it displays as its value, so a date part named by its aria-label still announces its selected option.

A theme or form whose FieldTemplate draws the description below the select or the help above it declares the order in fieldTemplateOrder in its presentation, and one whose SelectWidget draws the field's description itself, with its selected option's description before it, declares selectedOptionDescription: 'beforeDescription', so a screen reader announces them in the order they are shown (#5367, #5720).

widgetAriaProps() also names a select no label names, such as an untitled root or array item select, by its ui:placeholder, else TranslatableString.SelectPlaceholder ("Select ..."), since a select shows its value rather than a name (#5711). A replacement SelectWidget that draws its field's label itself, as widgetDrawsLabelText(props) says, takes no such name, since that label names the select; one whose plan has it draw its label must draw it, or the select is left with no name. So must a custom ui:field that hands its presentation on to the registry's SelectWidget, since that plan has the field draw the label: it draws one or passes the widget an aria-label. getGroupAttributes() names a radiogroup no label names the same way, by its ui:placeholder, else TranslatableString.RadioGroupName ("Choose an option"), where the widget passes it its label, placeholder and registry, as every theme's RadioWidget does; a replacement RadioWidget should pass them too (#5586). controlNameTests(Form) from @rjsf/snapshot-tests checks all of these against a theme's Form.

AltDateWidget hands an unset date part on as undefined, and useAltDateWidgetProps() returns buttonsDisabled BREAKING CHANGE​

useAltDateWidgetProps()'s elements give a part nobody has picked yet an undefined value, where the DateObject behind them holds -1, and DateElement hands the SelectWidget undefined for a -1 it is given (#5378). Every theme's parts now report it to onFocus and onBlur as undefined, as @rjsf/core's, @rjsf/react-bootstrap's and @rjsf/mantine's already did, where @rjsf/chakra-ui's reported '' and the other themes' -1. A replacement SelectWidget, a custom AltDateWidget that renders its own controls from elements, or an onBlur handler, that tells an unset part by '' or -1 should tell it by undefined.

useAltDateWidgetProps() returns buttonsDisabled, true when the widget is disabled or read-only, a required member of UseAltDateWidgetResult, so a hand-built one, such as a mocked return of the hook, has to include it (#5378).

enumOptionValueEncoder() is removed in favor of enumOptionsDomValues() BREAKING CHANGE​

enumOptionValueEncoder() encoded one option at a time, but in the realValue format an option's DOM value now depends on the rest of the list: options whose String() is the same, such as 1 and '1' or true and 'true', used to share a DOM value, so the second of them could not be picked and picking it wrote the first one's value (#5315). The new enumOptionsDomValues() encodes the whole list in one pass, giving each of those options its prefixed index (__rjsf_index:1) instead, and enumOptionValueDecoder() and enumOptionSelectedValue() encode against the list the same way. It also encodes an object, array, null or empty string option, and a string starting with the prefix, as its index prefixed with __rjsf_index:, where v6 encoded objects and arrays as the bare index and null as the empty string, so code that parses these DOM values itself needs to expect the prefix (#5309).

A custom widget encodes its options once per render and reads each option's value at its position:

// v6
value={enumOptionValueEncoder(option.value, index, optionValueFormat)}
// v7
const domValues = enumOptionsDomValues(enumOptions, optionValueFormat);
// ...
value={domValues[index]}

For options from groupEnumOptions(), read domValues[option.index], since index is the option's position in the ungrouped list.

@rjsf/utils schema functions take a SchemaContext in place of the validator BREAKING CHANGE​

The validator-based schema functions in @rjsf/utils used to take the customMergeAllOf and defaultFormStateBehavior of a form as separate parameters. Each of those functions had to copy them, one by one, into every schema function it called, and several calls left one out, so a customMergeAllOf silently stopped applying partway down a call chain (#4383, #4385).

Those settings now travel together with the validator in a SchemaContext:

interface SchemaContext<S extends StrictRJSFSchema = RJSFSchema, F extends FormContextType = FormContextType> {
  readonly validator: ValidatorType<S, F>;
  readonly customMergeAllOf?: CustomMergeAllOf<S>;
  readonly defaultFormStateBehavior?: DefaultFormStateBehavior;
}

Every function that took a validator takes a SchemaContext in its place, and passes it along whole to every schema function it calls, so dropping the customMergeAllOf would also mean dropping the validator. The separate customMergeAllOf and defaultFormStateBehavior parameters are gone, and the parameters that followed them move up a position; every other parameter, rootSchema included, is unchanged:

-const resolvedSchema = retrieveSchema(validator, schema, rootSchema, formData, customMergeAllOf);
-const isSelectField = isSelect(validator, schema, rootSchema, customMergeAllOf);
+const context: SchemaContext = { validator, customMergeAllOf, defaultFormStateBehavior };
+const resolvedSchema = retrieveSchema(context, schema, rootSchema, formData);
+const isSelectField = isSelect(context, schema, rootSchema);
Functionv6 parametersv7 parameters
findFieldInSchema()validator, rootSchema, schema, path, formData?, customMergeAllOf?context, rootSchema, schema, path, formData?
findSelectedOptionInXxxOf()validator, rootSchema, schema, fallbackField, xxx, formData?, customMergeAllOf?context, rootSchema, schema, fallbackField, xxx, formData?
getClosestMatchingOption()validator, rootSchema, formData, options, selectedOption?, discriminatorField?, customMergeAllOf?context, rootSchema, formData, options, selectedOption?, discriminatorField?
getDisplayLabel()validator, schema, uiSchema?, rootSchema?, globalOptions?, customMergeAllOf?context, schema, uiSchema?, rootSchema?, globalOptions?
getFirstMatchingOption()validator, formData, options, rootSchema, discriminatorField?context, formData, options, rootSchema, discriminatorField?
getFromSchema()validator, rootSchema, schema, path, defaultValue, customMergeAllOf?context, rootSchema, schema, path, defaultValue
getUiRequiredErrorSchema()new in v7context, rootSchema, uiSchema, formData, uiSchemaDefinitions?, globalUiOptions?, formContext?, fieldState?
isFilesArray()validator, schema, uiSchema?, rootSchema?, customMergeAllOf?context, schema, uiSchema?, rootSchema?
isMultiSelect()validator, schema, rootSchema?, customMergeAllOf?context, schema, rootSchema?
isSelect()validator, theSchema, rootSchema?, customMergeAllOf?context, theSchema, rootSchema?
omitExtraData()validator, schema, rootSchema?, formData?, customMergeAllOf?context, schema, rootSchema?, formData?, fieldState?
retrieveSchema()validator, schema, rootSchema?, rawFormData?, customMergeAllOf?, resolveAnyOfOrOneOfRefs?context, schema, rootSchema?, rawFormData?, resolveAnyOfOrOneOfRefs?, selectedOption?
sanitizeDataForNewSchema()validator, rootSchema, newSchema?, oldSchema?, data?, customMergeAllOf?context, rootSchema, newSchema?, oldSchema?, data?

retrieveSchema() is the one to double check: a v6 call passing resolveAnyOfOrOneOfRefs passed customMergeAllOf (or undefined) before it, so drop that argument rather than only replacing the validator.

getDefaultFormState() is the exception: it had the longest list of optional parameters, most of them easy to pass in the wrong order, so it now takes a SchemaContext followed by a GetDefaultFormStateProps object:

-getDefaultFormState(validator, schema, formData, rootSchema, false, defaultFormStateBehavior, customMergeAllOf, undefined, uiSchema);
+getDefaultFormState({ validator, customMergeAllOf, defaultFormStateBehavior }, { schema, formData, rootSchema, uiSchema });

Its props are schema, formData?, rootSchema?, includeUndefinedValues?, initialDefaultsGenerated?, uiSchema? and uiSchemaDefinitions?, with the same meanings and defaults the positional parameters had.

createSchemaUtils() and SchemaUtilsType.doesSchemaUtilsDiffer() take a SchemaContext and the rootSchema:

-const schemaUtils = createSchemaUtils(validator, rootSchema, defaultFormStateBehavior, customMergeAllOf);
+const schemaUtils = createSchemaUtils({ validator, defaultFormStateBehavior, customMergeAllOf }, rootSchema);

SchemaUtilsType's own methods supply the context and root schema themselves, so they are unchanged.

validateFormData(), isValid() and rawValidation() of ValidatorType take no SchemaContext, as in v6. rawValidation() changed in another way; see any members of the public types are specific types. A custom validator still has to change for this release, since isValid() is now handed { $ref } pointers into the rootSchema it is passed; see Validators are handed pointers into the root schema. The context carries a validator, so handing one to a validator would have meant every implementation discarding the validator it was given in favor of itself; the two things a validator actually needed the settings for are supplied another way instead.

validateFormData() takes one new optional trailing parameter, getCustomValidateFormData: a function returning the form data to hand customValidate, with the defaults already applied. Form supplies it from its own SchemaUtils, so those defaults honor the form's customMergeAllOf and defaultFormStateBehavior, which they never did before. Left out, the validator computes them itself exactly as it did in v6, so a direct caller keeps working:

 validator.validateFormData(formData, schema, customValidate, transformErrors, uiSchema);
+validator.validateFormData(formData, schema, customValidate, transformErrors, uiSchema, () => schemaUtils.getDefaultFormState(schema, formData, true, undefined, uiSchema));

It is a function rather than the data itself for two reasons: defaults that legitimately come out undefined are then an answer the validator can tell apart from "nothing was supplied", and an implementation that computes the defaults its own way never makes the caller compute them as well.

A precompiled validator takes the form's customMergeAllOf at construction rather than per call, since it is tied to one root schema compiled once:

-const validator = createPrecompiledValidator(validateFns, schema);
+const validator = createPrecompiledValidator(validateFns, schema, { customMergeAllOf });

It is used when the validator resolves its own root schema to check the schema it is handed, which is what previously failed with "The schema associated with the precompiled validator differs from the rootSchema provided for validation" for a form with a customMergeAllOf and an allOf in its root schema. compileSchemaValidators() and compileSchemaValidatorsCode() take no customMergeAllOf: they compile the subschemas the root names, and a schema a merge makes is not compiled (see Validators are handed pointers into the root schema).

The computeSkipPopulate() callback of defaultFormStateBehavior.arrayMinItems receives the SchemaContext in effect in place of the validator, so any schema function it calls can be handed the form's customMergeAllOf too:

-computeSkipPopulate: (validator, schema, rootSchema) => !isSelect(validator, schema.items, rootSchema),
+computeSkipPopulate: (context, schema, rootSchema) => !isSelect(context, schema.items, rootSchema),

The helpers @rjsf/utils exported only through deep imports of lib/schema/*, such as computeDefaults() and calculateIndexScore(), can no longer be imported, since deep imports are removed.

Four places that used to drop a setting now apply it:

  • SchemaUtilsType.omitExtraData() never passed the form's customMergeAllOf on, so the allOfs it merged were always merged the default way.
  • An allOf reached through a $ref option of a oneOf inside dependencies was always merged the default way.
  • The defaults handed to customValidate were computed with neither the customMergeAllOf nor the defaultFormStateBehavior of the form.
  • The precompiled validators of @rjsf/validator-ajv8 and @rjsf/validator-ata check the schema they are handed against their root schema, resolving that root schema when it isn't an exact match. They resolved it with the default allOf merge, so under liveValidate a form with a customMergeAllOf and an allOf in its root schema failed with "The schema associated with the precompiled validator differs from the rootSchema provided for validation". They now resolve it with the customMergeAllOf they were constructed with, so the error no longer comes from validateFormData(), nor from a schema function scoring oneOf/anyOf options or resolving a condition against that root schema.

A form that sets either of them sees it applied in those places from now on.

With a precompiled validator, give the form's customMergeAllOf to createPrecompiledValidator(), as above, so the root-schema check resolves with the merge the form resolves with.

findSelectedOptionInXxxOf() returns the closest option for options with no discriminator BREAKING CHANGE​

findSelectedOptionInXxxOf() returned undefined for options with no discriminator unless the data held the value of a default or const one of them declared (#5392). It now returns the option getClosestMatchingOption() picks for the data, as MultiSchemaField does, and no longer reads fallbackField. With no data that is the first option, and a tie goes to the first option the data matches, or to the first option when it matches none. Options with a discriminator read as before, so a value none of them holds selects nothing.

What to change: code that reads undefined as "no option is selected" for such options now gets an option, so it should look for what it wants in that option. Options told apart by the value of a property should name it as their discriminator, the only property read by value now.

 const option = schemaUtils.findSelectedOptionInXxxOf(schema, 'a', 'anyOf', formData);
-if (option) {
+if (option?.properties?.a) {

A LayoutGridField cell naming a property beside anyOf/oneOf, or of options with no discriminator, renders the field BREAKING CHANGE​

A LayoutGridField cell { name: 'a', render: Comp } whose name is a property declared beside anyOf/oneOf, or a property of options with no discriminator, showed Comp, since the grid read the cell only from the selected option and found no schema for it (#5392). The grid now reads a property beside the options from there, and a property of the options from the option the form shows, so the cell renders the field and leaves Comp out, as a cell naming a plain property does. To keep showing Comp, name no property:

-{ name: 'a', render: Comp }
+{ name: '', render: Comp }

A LayoutGridField on the schema holding options with no discriminator is the exception: while MultiSchemaField renders the options beside the grid, the option there renders its own properties, so a cell naming one of them still renders nothing, or its render. For { properties: { x: { type: 'string' } }, anyOf: [{ properties: { a: { type: 'string' } } }, { properties: { b: { type: 'number' } } }] } with { a: 'q' }, a row of x and a renders root_x, then the option selector and the option's root_a.

To have the grid lay out the option's properties instead, set ui:fieldReplacesAnyOrOneOf so the grid replaces the options. It then renders no option selector and the data decides which option its cells read when the form gets it, which then holds while the user edits a cell, as it does outside a grid, so a user can't choose another option, and a row without b shows nothing for { b: 1 }:

 {
   'ui:field': 'LayoutGridField',
+  'ui:fieldReplacesAnyOrOneOf': true,
   'ui:layoutGrid': { /* ... */ },
 }

A LayoutGridField cell naming a property of discriminated options beside the grid renders nothing BREAKING CHANGE​

A LayoutGridField on the schema holding discriminated anyOf/oneOf options, without ui:fieldReplacesAnyOrOneOf, rendered a cell for the selected option's property while MultiSchemaField rendered the options beside the grid, so two inputs shared an id (#5747). The option beside the grid now renders its property alone, and the cell renders nothing, or its render, as it does for options with no discriminator. For { discriminator: { propertyName: 'kind' }, properties: { x: { type: 'string' } }, oneOf: [{ properties: { kind: { const: 'a' }, a: { type: 'string' } } }, { properties: { kind: { const: 'b' }, b: { type: 'number' } } }] } with { kind: 'a', a: 'q' }, a row of x and a renders root_x, then the option selector and the option's root_a.

What to change: to have the grid lay out the option's properties, set ui:fieldReplacesAnyOrOneOf so the grid replaces the options, as for options with no discriminator. Otherwise remove a cell naming only the property, which renders nothing; a { name, render } cell still shows its render.

A property declared beside anyOf/oneOf and in an option is read from beside them BREAKING CHANGE​

findFieldInSchema() and a LayoutGridField cell read a property that a schema declares both beside its anyOf/oneOf and in an option from the option. They now read it from beside the options (#5392).

For { properties: { kind: { enum: ['a', 'b'] } }, oneOf: [{ properties: { kind: { const: 'a' } }, required: ['kind'] }, { properties: { kind: { const: 'b' } } }] } with { kind: 'a' }, findFieldInSchema() returned { const: 'a' } as required, and now returns the enum as not required, and a grid cell renders the enum.

What to change: declare the property in one place, or add it to the required list beside the options. A property only an option declares is read as before.

 {
   properties: { kind: { enum: ['a', 'b'] } },
+  required: ['kind'],
   oneOf: [
     { properties: { kind: { const: 'a' } }, required: ['kind'] },
     { properties: { kind: { const: 'b' } } },
   ],
 }

A custom ObjectFieldTemplate asks registry.schemaUtils.canExpand() BREAKING CHANGE​

Whether an object naming no additionalProperties takes extra keys is now a form setting, additionalPropertiesWhenAbsent, which travels in the SchemaContext (#2137). SchemaUtilsType gains canExpand(schema, uiSchema, formData) and allowsAdditionalProperties(schema), which pass the form's own SchemaContext, every theme's ObjectFieldTemplate now calls registry.schemaUtils.canExpand(), and @rjsf/utils no longer exports canExpand() itself (see Utilities no other RJSF package uses are no longer exported from @rjsf/utils).

A custom ObjectFieldTemplate does the same:

// v6
{canExpand(schema, uiSchema, formData) && <AddButton onClick={onAddProperty} />}
// v7
{registry.schemaUtils.canExpand(schema, uiSchema, formData) && <AddButton onClick={onAddProperty} />}

A SchemaUtilsType implementation of your own needs the two new methods.

An $id under an unknown keyword, such as components or x-*, names no schema BREAKING CHANGE​

Embedded schemas are found by $id through the schema's structure: only the keywords that hold a schema, an array of schemas or a map of names to schemas are walked. Under a container that is none of these, such as an OpenAPI-style components block or an x-* vendor key, an $id is data. It is no longer found as an embedded schema, and it no longer changes what the $refs beside and below it resolve against, also where a $ref reaches the schema holding it. A schema such a $ref reaches is still read as a schema, and its own $refs resolve against the resource holding the container, so the usual OpenAPI layout, with components at the root and #/components/... refs, keeps working. Only one case breaks: a $ref to an $id declared inside the container, which now throws Could not find a definition for .... If a schema relies on it, move those schemas under $defs (draft 2020-12) or definitions (draft 7) so the walk reaches them. A $ref beside such an $id resolves where it threw: with $defs: { real: { $id: 'n.json', type: 'boolean' }, s: { type: 'string' } }, components: { Pet: { type: 'object', properties: { n: { $id: 'n.json', $ref: '#/$defs/s' } } } } and properties: { pet: { $ref: '#/components/Pet' } } under a root whose $id is https://e.com/root.json, root_pet_n is a string field, where the form threw Could not find a definition for #/$defs/s..

One symptom is worth knowing: AJV collects $ids by walking every key, so it still finds an $id kept under components or x-*. A form whose schema relies on that passes validation but throws Could not find a definition for ... when it renders.

localToUTC() can return null BREAKING CHANGE​

localToUTC() takes unknown and returns string | null | undefined, where its inferred return type was string | undefined. null isn't a new result: localToUTC() has always returned it for a value Date can't read, since toJSON() gives null for an invalid date though its type says string. A value Date throws for, such as a bigint or a symbol, now gives null as well instead of throwing. Code that assigns the result to string | undefined no longer compiles; map null to the value it should store:

// Before
const utc: string | undefined = localToUTC(value);

// After
const utc: string | undefined = localToUTC(value) ?? undefined;

A non-object field's anyOf/oneOf option renders with its parent's keywords BREAKING CHANGE​

A field with anyOf/oneOf options is rendered entirely by its selected option, unless it is an object, whose own ObjectField renders its properties beside the option. A type list naming object, such as ['object', 'string'] or a nullable ['object', 'null'], counts as an object only while the option shown can hold one, so an option of another type, a null option included, renders the whole field wherever object sits in the list rather than beside the object's properties (#5725). The option used to inherit only the field's required list and type, so anything else the field declared never reached the control that renders it (#5359). An array whose options only limit its length rendered "Unsupported field schema ... Missing items definition." in place of its items, and a format: 'date' string rendered a plain text input.

{
  "type": "array",
  "items": { "type": "string", "enum": ["a", "b"] },
  "uniqueItems": true,
  "oneOf": [{ "minItems": 1 }, { "maxItems": 1 }]
}

The option of a field that is not an object now inherits every keyword of the field that describes its value, so this schema renders a multi-select. That includes keywords that change how a field that already rendered looks, such as format, enum, examples and readOnly, so a format: 'date' string now renders a date input. Switching to another option checks the value against that option as it renders, inherited keywords included, so an array whose options only limit its length keeps its items, where checking it against the bare option, which is no array, cleared them. A value that is neither an array nor an object, such as a string, is still cleared by every switch, even between two options that both describe it. A tuple keeps its items the same way, each sanitized against the schema the selected option declares at its position, unless the selected option gives a prefix position a type that leaves out one the other option gave it, which clears the array; an item past them is dropped instead. An array the selected option has a const for is replaced with that const when it doesn't equal it, as one the option selects whole arrays from with an enum is cleared when the enum doesn't list it, unless the option switched away from declared the same const or enum, which already rejected the array. Where both options render the items alike, with the same uiSchema and a field per item, and the switch leaves the array's length as it was, an item field's own errors stay with the item, as its field stays in place. An option that is a select over whole arrays renders one control for the array, and one holding options of its own renders its items anew, so a switch to or from either drops them. The field's title, description, deprecated and default stay with the field rather than being repeated on the option. The field's own template labels it and draws its description whichever option is selected, an array or a checkbox included, and the option's field draws its own title and description only where they say something else, as a field's label, description, help and errors are drawn where its plan says describes. A bound both the field and the option declare, such as maxItems, maxLength or minimum, keeps the stricter of the two, since a value has to meet both: an option's maxItems: 5 beside the field's maxItems: 3 stops Add at three items, and switching to that option trims the array to three. An option's true subschema, such as items: true, adds nothing to meet, so it leaves the field's subschema in place rather than rendering every item as an unsupported field, a tuple included. An option's items schema beside the field's tuple applies to each of its positions, and to the items past it where the tuple declares additionalItems; a tuple declaring none stays at its length, as ArrayField offers it no Add, and so does an option's tuple beside the field's items schema. A field's false subschema, which nothing meets, stays in place of the option's in the same way. An enum the option declares is its own list as it stands, since its ui:enumNames are read by position against it: a value the field's enum doesn't list stays, and validation rejects it. Two required lists ask for every name either does. A not, or a conditional (if, then and else together), that the option declares replaces the field's as a whole, rather than being merged with it into one neither declared. Any other keyword both declare, such as a format or a pattern, is the option's. A subschema either declares through a $ref, such as items: { "$ref": "#/$defs/short" }, is left to the field's allOf merge, which meets the two once the $ref is resolved: met before it, the keywords beside the $ref would be layered over the ones it names, and a looser bound would win. ui:required is checked against the option as it renders, too: a ui:required field within the field's items is checked where an option's items: true leaves them in place, and one the field's false subschema forbids is not. The form's defaults are computed from the option as it renders as well, so an option's minItems: 1 beside the field's minItems: 2 starts the form with two items, each holding the defaults of the field's items, whether the option is written in place or as a $ref, and a tuple's options add to the defaults of its positions. An option written as a $ref is followed only to the schema it names, so an allOf within it is still left to the allOf defaults behavior. One that inherits nothing from the field, such as the option of a typeless field, is computed as before, taking the field's default only when there is no data; one that inherits something takes the field's default as an option written in place does, beneath its data and its own default. A field that is not an object and declares both anyOf and oneOf renders only the selected option of the keyword SchemaField reads, the anyOf unless it is empty, so its defaults are that option's alone, where they used to include those of the other keyword's selected option too. An object field still adds both. The bounds are read as draft-06 and later define them, where exclusiveMinimum and exclusiveMaximum are numbers of their own. The draft-04 form, a boolean that makes minimum or maximum exclusive, is not supported: beside a numeric bound from the other schema it can make a bound exclusive that neither schema did, as with a field's maximum: 3 and an option's { maximum: 5, exclusiveMaximum: true }, which renders as less than 3. A schema written for draft-04 or OpenAPI 3.0 should use the numeric form, exclusiveMaximum: 5 in place of maximum: 5, exclusiveMaximum: true.

An object that names no type of its own, but has properties, now passes object on to options that name no type either, as a type: 'object' field already did. Its options used to render "Unsupported field schema ... Unknown field type undefined."; they now render as the typed field's do.

An option selector stays a select for a text, updown or range ui:widget its options inherit BREAKING CHANGE​

This affects a field with non-constant anyOf/oneOf options, a ui:widget of text, updown or range (or TextWidget, UpDownWidget or RangeWidget), and at least one option with no uiSchema entry of its own. The option selector rendered that widget too, showing the selected option's index as a number to edit. It now stays a select, and the widget renders only on an option that inherits it. Any other widget, such as radio, stays on the selector as it was.

To keep such a widget on the selector, give every option a uiSchema entry, so that none of them inherits it:

 const uiSchema = {
   'ui:widget': 'range',
+  anyOf: [{}, {}],
 };

See Multiple types for details.

An anyOf/oneOf option naming no type takes its field's type for the Optional Data Controls BREAKING CHANGE​

The Optional Data Controls (enableOptionalDataFieldForType) read the type of a field with anyOf/oneOf options from the options alone, so a field whose options named no type of their own never got them, whatever its own type said (#5360).

{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": { "a": { "type": "string" }, "b": { "type": "string" } },
  "oneOf": [{ "required": ["a"] }, { "required": ["b"] }]
}

An option naming no type now takes the field's own, as the option MultiSchemaField renders already did, so with object enabled this optional field renders behind an Add button, and nothing else until it is clicked, where it used to show its fields and the option selector straight away. An optional array whose anyOf options are minItems/maxItems bounds already rendered an Add button with array enabled, since its option took the array's type, but showed the option selector beside it; now it hides the selector until Add is clicked, unless its defaults fill it, as the first option's minItems: 1 does under the default arrayMinItems, which renders it with its items and a Remove button, as a plain minItems array does. Options naming several types still get none, a null option beside another type included, since such a list keeps the selector the null branch is reached through, which the controls would hide: { "type": ["object", "null"], "anyOf": [{ "required": ["a"] }, { "type": "null" }] } renders as before, while the same field with every option typeless resolves to object and gets the controls. ui:required follows: a ui:required property of such an object is not reported while the object has no value, since its properties are hidden behind the Add button then. So do the form's defaults: while such an object has no value, none of the nulls of its type: 'null' properties is filled in, so it stays out of the defaults. To keep the old rendering, leave the field's type out of enableOptionalDataFieldForType, or set ui:enableOptionalDataFieldForType to [] in that field's uiSchema to turn the controls off for that field alone. Marking the field ui:required would render it as before too, but it also keeps the form from submitting while the field is empty.

An empty object counts as added data for the Optional Data Controls BREAKING CHANGE​

With enableOptionalDataFieldForType naming object, an optional object holding {} counted as having no data, so it rendered behind its Add button, and an Add that stored {}, as one for an object with only additionalProperties does, changed nothing (#5427). isFormDataAvailable() now returns true for {}, so only undefined and null count as no data. An object holding {} renders its fields and a Remove button, a ui:required property of it is reported, and its type: 'null' properties get their nulls in the defaults, as any added object's do. An anyOf/oneOf switch no longer writes {} for an optional object in the new option, array items included, that the old data held nothing for, so it stays behind its Add button, as when the form mounts on that option. An object with anyOf/oneOf options renders one set of controls, its own, in its heading beside the options, root_n__XxxOf__optionalAdd. The selected option drew a second set, root_n__optionalAdd, which an object with neither properties of its own nor room for more keys besides its options still draws, since nothing renders beside them. Until Add, the selected option of an object with properties of its own or room for more keys renders nothing, where it drew an empty frame titled after the option, or its fields where its own uiSchema turned the controls off, so typing in them added the object. With neither an option selector nor an option to show, the field renders no MultiSchemaFieldTemplate at all, so a custom one that draws something around its selector and optionSchemaField, such as a wrapper or a heading, renders it only after Add. omitExtraData still drops an optional object holding {}, so with it set an added object that holds nothing goes back behind its Add button on submit, and under liveOmit="onChange" its Add still does nothing. To keep an optional object behind its Add button, leave it out of the data rather than setting it to {}:

- initialFormData={{ meta: {} }}
+ initialFormData={{}}

Code that called isFormDataAvailable() to tell an empty object from a filled one should check Object.keys(formData).length > 0 itself.

A field's label, description, help and errors are drawn where its plan says BREAKING CHANGE​

SchemaField now plans each field before rendering it (#5490): from the field and widget it renders, and the presentation the registry merges from @rjsf/core, the theme and the Form, it decides who draws the field's label, description, help and errors, under which ids, and the attributes its control carries. The plan reaches the FieldTemplate, the field and its widget as a presentation prop, as described in resolveFieldPresentation(), and the props templates and widgets already read are now derived from it. displayLabel, rawErrors, hideLabel and getDisplayLabel() are marked @deprecated and kept through v7 for a template or widget rendered without a plan; read the plan instead, or templateDrawsLabel(), widgetDrawsLabel() and hasWidgetErrors(), which fall back to them only without one. The rawErrors a field and an ArrayFieldTemplate or ObjectFieldTemplate are handed, which carry the errors whatever hideError says, and hasVisibleErrors(), which applies hideError to them, are marked @deprecated too, with VisibleErrorsProps, its parameter type (#5325): the plan's presentation.errors.messages has ui:hideError applied, and a widget or container template draws them only where presentation.errors.by is 'self', since the template draws them under 'template', which is what the new getErrorsToDraw() gives it; a field reads presentation.errors.messages itself, since getErrorsToDraw() gives a field that draws its own errors none, so that a widget it spreads its plan into doesn't draw them again; for an error state, read hasWidgetErrors() for a widget's control and fieldShowsOwnErrors() for the label or description a widget draws for its field, hasErrors in a FieldTemplate, ArrayFieldTemplate or ObjectFieldTemplate, or presentation.errors.own in a field. All four stay through v7, and the props are still handed over in full, for a component that renders the hidden errors its own way. With a plan, the plan wins: core's and every theme's templates and widgets ignore a hideLabel, displayLabel or rawErrors handed alongside one, so a custom field that renders a widget with its plan and hideLabel to hide the widget's label should hand it a plan whose label isn't the widget's instead:

  • displayLabel is true only where the template draws the label. In a theme whose widgets draw their own label, as @rjsf/mui's, @rjsf/fluentui-rc's, @rjsf/chakra-ui's and @rjsf/mantine's do, it is false for nearly every field, so a custom FieldTemplate there should no longer gate the description on it. Read it through templateDrawsLabel(), which reads the plan and falls back to displayLabel only for a template rendered without one.
  • ArrayFieldItemTemplateProps.displayLabel says whether a label sits above the item's control, from the plan the item's SchemaField builds, where it was getDisplayLabel() of the item's schema and its own uiSchema: a label its template draws, which is the displayLabel the item's own FieldTemplate is handed, or one its field or widget draws itself where its declaration places it labelPlacement: 'above', as @rjsf/fluentui-rc, @rjsf/chakra-ui and @rjsf/mantine declare their widgets' labels. So the item's buttons are placed by the label above its control. It is now false for an item with no label text, a null item, a hidden item, a boolean under ui:widget: 'checkbox', and a custom field drawing its own label whichever of ui:field or a $id names it, unless its declaration places that label above, and true for a custom field declared { label: 'template' }, a boolean whose titled oneOf constants render a select, and an object anyOf/oneOf, whose selector its template labels, as does an item the fallback UI (useFallbackUiForUnsupportedType) renders with a choice of types, whose type selector comes first and is labelled for the type whatever the item's title, unless ui:label is false or the item is hidden, which hides the selector with it. In @rjsf/mui, whose text inputs and selects draw their label inside the input's outline, it is false for those.
  • description and rawDescription, help and rawHelp, and errors are handed to the template only where it draws them. Render them when they are present rather than deciding again from displayLabel or the uiSchema.
  • hideLabel tells a widget that the template, or a field above rendering the same id, draws its label. A widget that keyed its own description on hideLabel should take it from getWidgetDescription() instead, and one that draws its own label should ask widgetDrawsLabel(), which falls back to hideLabel only for a widget rendered without a plan.
  • required still says whether the field is required; a template drawing the label should mark it from presentation.label.requiredMarker, as @rjsf/core's does, which leaves the * off a checkbox, or a widget its theme declares uncheckedIsFalse, whose schema doesn't demand true, unless ui:required: true asks for it while it holds no value (#5388), or an array rendered as one widget, such as a group of checkboxes or a multiple select, holding [] while its schema has no minItems of at least 1 (#5573, #5744).
  • A template drawing the label should give it the for that templateLabelFor() gives, as @rjsf/core's does, which is none where presentation.control.attributes['aria-labelledby'] is set: that control, such as the wrapper of a group of radios or checkboxes, is one a for can't name, and it is named through the label's presentation.label.id instead.

What renders differently:

  • anyOf/oneOf. The field's template labels the field and draws its description, help and errors, whichever option is selected, so the option's control no longer draws a second label (#5358) and the errors no longer disappear with a null option. An option's own title and description render beneath the field's only where they say something else, the description under optionDescriptionId(). An option given no uiSchema of its own no longer takes the field's ui:title and ui:description in place of its own. An option with no title of its own takes the field's label rather than its property name: as its control's label in a theme whose selector draws the field's label itself, as @rjsf/mui's, @rjsf/chakra-ui's, @rjsf/fluentui-rc's and @rjsf/mantine's do, and as its heading while an optional data control keeps the selector off screen, with the field's description beneath that heading. An object with no properties of its own beside its options is labelled as the field rendering those options is; one with properties keeps drawing its heading, under the XxxOf ids it renders beside the options with. As in v6, the option selector isn't required, even for a required field, since it picks an option index rather than a value and holds one unless its widget offers an empty choice (#5527). No built-in selector does, except @rjsf/mantine's where the field's ui:options set allowDeselect or clearable, and clearing the choice clears the field's data with it. A required field shows one *, on the field's own label, whichever option is selected and whether its template or its selector draws that label (#5573). The selected option's own label or heading stays unmarked, and its control stays required. So ObjectFieldTemplate's and ArrayFieldTemplate's required now says whether the heading they draw is marked, which a template using it for anything else should read from the schema instead, and a custom widget of @rjsf/mui, @rjsf/chakra-ui, @rjsf/fluentui-rc or @rjsf/mantine that hands required to a component drawing its label should mark that label from templateMarksRequired(), or it shows a second * beneath an anyOf/oneOf selector and none as that selector. Also as in v6, a discriminated cell a LayoutGridField lays out is required with its cell, since its selector is the only control for the discriminator it writes into the data, where an anyOf/oneOf field's selected option renders the discriminator as a control of its own.

  • Custom fields. A field given as ui:field or a $id draws its own label and description, as one given as ui:field already did: one chosen by a $id used to get the template's label. Declare the parts the template should draw for it under its registry key. A widget it renders with its props, plan included, draws none of the label, description and errors it draws itself (#5591), so one that left its label, description or errors to a widget such as CheckboxWidget declares WIDGET_FIELD_PRESENTATION under its key, or draws them itself. A custom field is handed its own plan as presentation, so one that spreads its props into a field it renders itself, such as StringField, should leave presentation out of them, or that field takes the custom field's label and ids for its own. One that renders SchemaField under its own id, as a wrapper adding markup around the field does, leaves the label and description it was planned to draw to the field it renders, which draws them, while its template draws the help and errors once. A template label declared through fieldDefault would also reach objects and arrays, which have no control for the template's label to name, so they would draw no heading:

    <Form presentation={{ fields: { MyField: { label: 'template', description: 'template' } } }} />

  • ui:label: false hides the description along with the label in every theme, as it already did outside @rjsf/antd.

  • An empty ui:title or ui:description on an object no longer hides its heading or description: the schema's title or description shows instead, as it already did for an array and for a field whose template draws its label. Set ui:label: false to hide both.

  • null fields, and a field rendered through UnsupportedFieldTemplate, draw their own title and description, through TitleFieldTemplate and DescriptionFieldTemplate, rather than a label naming no control.

  • The fallback UI labels its value from outside only where the value is a single control; an object, an array or a checkbox value draws its own heading or label, with the field's description beneath it, as before.

  • A required group of checkboxes shows a * and tells a screen reader it is required only where its schema demands a checked box, with a minItems of at least 1, or where ui:required: true asks for it (#5573). required alone leaves an empty array valid, as the form submitted [] with nothing checked, so such a group shows no *, and its widget's required is false: add minItems: 1 to keep them, which also has the form demand a box. The group's accessible name then ends in "required" (TranslatableString.RequiredGroupCue), so a test finding it by name, such as getByRole('group', { name: 'Colors' }), should expect Colors required. A custom checkboxes widget calling getGroupAttributes() passes the registry and renders the requiredCue it returns, or its name stays as it was, as does one calling @rjsf/daisyui's getGroupAndOptionProps(), which takes the registry and returns the requiredCue alike, while getGroupProps() returns no cue. Only minItems and ui:required are read: a required group with no minItems shows no * or cue though a contains rejects [], so the form blocks that submit; give such a group minItems: 1 or ui:required: true. A group holding no value, as emptyObjectFields: 'skipEmptyDefaults' leaves it, keeps its * and cue, since the form rejects that. An anyOf/oneOf field follows the option shown: a required field shows no * while that option holds the [] of such a group or the false of a checkbox whose schema accepts it.

  • A required multiple select, file input or custom array widget is required, by its * and the required its widget is handed, only where its schema has a minItems of at least 1 or ui:required: true asks for it, as a group of checkboxes is (#5744). getDefaultFormState() seeds a required array with [], which required alone accepts, and a <select multiple>'s native required had the browser block that submit, so the form called neither onSubmit nor onError. A form that relied on that to force a choice adds minItems: 1, which also has the form report an empty selection, and a custom array widget reads its required prop rather than assuming one. As for a group, one holding no value, as emptyObjectFields: 'skipEmptyDefaults' leaves it, stays required, since the form rejects that. An array rendered as a list of items keeps its *.

  • Labels a widget draws take the field's label as the template's does: an array item whose items schema has a title is labelled by it rather than by the numbered title (Tags-1), and a deprecated field's carries the DeprecatedLabel marker.

  • Headings. @rjsf/core's TitleFieldTemplate puts the titleId() it is handed on a <span> around the title's text rather than on its <legend>, since an object's option selector is named by that id and would otherwise take the * and the optional data control's button into its name. A selector or style aimed at legend#root__title should aim at legend #root__title, and a custom TitleFieldTemplate should put its id on the title's text alone.

  • Group labels. @rjsf/core's FieldTemplate draws the label of a RadioWidget or CheckboxesWidget with no for, which named the group's wrapper <div>, an element a for can't label; the group is named by the label's fieldLabelId() through aria-labelledby. A selector aimed at label[for="root_color"] for such a field should aim at #root_color__label, which is on a <span> around the label's text, as a heading's id is, so a group named by it takes no *; label:has(#root_color__label) matches the label itself. RatingWidget renders its stars as a radiogroup on the wrapper <div>, named the same way, where its label's for named its hidden <input>; the wrapper carries the field's id in that <input>'s place, so a selector aimed at input#root_rating should aim at #root_rating. AltDateWidget, and so AltDateTimeWidget, wraps its list of date parts in a group <div> carrying the field's id, named the same way, around the <ul>, which keeps its list role, where its label's for named an id no date part carried, so a selector aimed at label[for="root_when"] should aim at #root_when__label. An anyOf/oneOf field has its label drawn with no for too while the option it shows renders no control at the field's id for a for to name, such as an object, an array of items or a null, renders a group such as AltDateWidget's, or renders options of its own, whose option shown may be an object, which is named by the label through aria-labelledby, as the option selector is whatever option is shown, so a selector aimed at label[for="root_pet"] for such a field should aim at #root_pet__label; while it shows an option rendering a single control, such as a string's input or an array's multi-select or file input, the label keeps the for. While it shows no option, as after its selector's empty choice is picked, the label has no for whatever its options are, since nothing renders at the field's id. Where AnyOfField or OneOfField is declared labelledBy: 'aria-labelledby', as presentation={{ fields: { OneOfField: { labelledBy: 'aria-labelledby' } } }} declares it, the label has no for whatever option shows, and a single control is named by it through aria-labelledby. An option given a ui:field counts as rendering a single control, so one wrapping an object keeps the for; to draw none, register the field under a key and declare labelledBy: 'aria-labelledby' for that key. A widget of your own registered as RadioWidget, CheckboxesWidget, RatingWidget, AltDateWidget or AltDateTimeWidget takes that declaration with the key, so it is named only through the aria-labelledby it spreads from getControlAttributes() or getGroupAttributes(); one that renders a single control under its id and spreads neither should be declared labelledBy: 'for' under its key, as presentation={{ widgets: { CheckboxesWidget: { labelledBy: 'for' } } }} declares one registered as CheckboxesWidget, to keep the label's for. One that draws its own label, such as a date picker registered as AltDateWidget, should be declared label: 'self' under its key, so the template draws no second label. @rjsf/antd declares its RangeWidget labelledBy: 'aria-labelledby', since a for reaches only the slider's root rather than its handle, so a widget of your own registered as RangeWidget under antd's theme takes that declaration too. A wrapper of antd's slider registered under a key of your own, or the slider itself registered under one while RangeWidget holds another widget, takes no declaration, so declare that key labelledBy: 'aria-labelledby' for its handle to be named; one passed to ui:widget as a component has no key to declare, so register it under one. Under antd, #root_color__label is likewise on a <span> around the label's text, which also carries the label's title, so label:has(#root_color__label) matches the label.

  • An untitled field has no label, so a required array item with no title no longer renders a label holding only the required marker; the input is still required.

  • additionalProperties. The key input is labelled wherever the entry's value is, whoever draws that label, so a checkbox entry's key is now labelled too, and where ui:label: false hides that label, the key input is named by it through aria-label. An object or array entry's heading shows its ui:title, or its schema title, where it has one, as before.

  • Layout grid anyOf/oneOf cells. A discriminated union a LayoutGridField lays out draws its label whatever its schema's type, as one with no type already did: one declaring type: 'object' beside its oneOf drew none, and left its selector unnamed. Set ui:label: false on the cell to hide it; the selector is still named by its text.

  • Accessibility. A control's aria-describedby names only elements that render, an AltDateWidget's parts included, it is aria-invalid while it has errors, except a radio, whose radiogroup is instead, the template's label carries fieldLabelId() on its text, and a group of radios or checkboxes is labelled by that label through aria-labelledby. A SelectWidget of your own describes an AltDateWidget's parts only by reading its props through widgetAriaProps(): DateElement hands it a plan of its own rather than an aria-describedby.

  • @rjsf/mantine's errors and RatingWidget. Errors its widgets don't show, those of a custom widget or ui:field, @rjsf/core's RatingWidget or a widget whose inputWrapperOrder leaves out 'error', are shown by FieldErrorTemplate, where they were announced from a hidden copy and never shown; see the Mantine ids section. A custom ui:field that hands one of this theme's widgets rawErrors but not its plan, as FieldProps.presentation advises for a field that doesn't declare WIDGET_FIELD_PRESENTATION, shows the field's errors twice: the widget, given no plan, draws them, and so does the template. Pass the widget hideError or no rawErrors, or declare WIDGET_FIELD_PRESENTATION for the field and hand the widget its presentation. The theme declares @rjsf/core's RatingWidget label: 'template' and description: 'template', since it draws neither, so a widget of your own registered as RatingWidget that draws its own label should be declared label: 'self' under that key, as the "Group labels" entry above says, and one that draws its own description description: 'self', or it shows them twice, or, where it draws its label only while widgetDrawsLabel() is true and spreads no aria-labelledby from getControlAttributes() or getGroupAttributes(), its control is left with no name.

  • @rjsf/chakra-ui's ids, RatingWidget and alt-date widgets. The element a user focuses carries the field's id rather than an id Ark generated: the text input, the textarea, the number input's and the checkbox's <input>, the select's trigger and the slider's thumb, and in a radio or checkboxes group, which carries the field's id itself, each <input> its optionId(). A selector aimed at an Ark id, such as select:root_color:trigger or checkbox:root_color-0:input, should aim at #root_color or the option's id. TitleField puts the title id on a <span> around the title's text inside its <h5> rather than on the box around the heading, its optional data control and its separator, so a selector or style aimed at #root__title now reaches that <span>. The select's label has no for, so a selector aimed at label[for="root_color"] should aim at #root_color__label, and a checkboxes group's label is drawn as a <div> styled as the fieldset's legend rather than as a <legend>, so a legend selector no longer reaches it. The theme declares @rjsf/core's RatingWidget and its own AltDateWidget and AltDateTimeWidget label: 'template', since none of them draws a label, so a widget of your own registered under one of those keys that draws its own label should be declared label: 'self' under its key, as the "Group labels" entry above says, or it shows two labels, or, where it draws its label only while widgetDrawsLabel() is true and spreads no aria-labelledby from getControlAttributes() or getGroupAttributes(), its control is left with no name.

  • @rjsf/daisyui's headings and triggers. TitleField puts the title id on a <span> around the title's text inside its <h2>, and ArrayFieldTitleTemplate on one inside its <h3>, each followed by a * for a required object or array, so a selector or style aimed at div#root__title or h3#root_tags__title should aim at #root__title or #root_tags__title. A radio, checkboxes, rating or alt-date field's label has no for, as @rjsf/core's doesn't, so a selector aimed at label[for="root_color"] should aim at label:has(#root_color__label). FieldTemplate's label puts its label id on a <span> around the label's text, for every field, as @rjsf/core's does, so a selector aimed at label#root_name__label should aim at label #root_name__label, which matches that <span>, or at label:has(#root_name__label) for the label together with its *. SelectWidget's trigger, like the date pickers', has the combobox role, so a query for it by the button role should use combobox. Both take the keys that role promises: Down Arrow, or Alt+Down Arrow, opens either, a date picker's moving focus onto its selected day, else today, and in SelectWidget Down and Up Arrow move into the listbox and between its options, Home and End to its first and last, from the trigger too, and Enter or Space on an option of a single select, or a click on one, chooses it and closes the listbox, as Escape does, returning focus to the trigger. The trigger is SelectWidget's one tab stop, so Tab moves on to the next field rather than through the options, and Shift+Tab from an option closes the listbox as it returns focus to the trigger. The listbox opens on daisyUI's :focus-within, so it stays open while focus is anywhere inside it, an option included, and closes once focus leaves it.

  • @rjsf/fluentui-rc's groups, required and headings. RadioWidget and CheckboxesWidget draw their label with no for, which named the radio group's wrapper or, for CheckboxesWidget, an id no element had, and name the group by it through aria-labelledby, so a selector aimed at label[for="root_color"] should aim at #root_color__label. FieldTemplate's Field no longer takes required, which Fluent handed every control inside it, so only the controls the plan marks are required, and a custom widget whose Fluent control took required from the Field sets it itself. TitleField puts the title id on a <span> inside its <h5>, so a selector aimed at div#root__title should aim at #root__title. SelectWidget draws no label holding only a required field's *, and a dropdown no label names carries an aria-label: the field's label, its placeholder or the translated prompt, so a snapshot of an untitled select gains it. The theme declares @rjsf/core's RatingWidget, AltDateWidget and AltDateTimeWidget label: 'template', since none of them draws a label, so a widget of your own registered under one of those keys that draws its own label should be declared label: 'self' under its key, as the "Group labels" entry above says, or it shows two labels, or, where it draws its label only while widgetDrawsLabel() is true and spreads no aria-labelledby from getControlAttributes() or getGroupAttributes(), its control is left with no name.

  • @rjsf/mui's slider, groups, headings and errors. RangeWidget puts the field's id on its slider's <input> rather than on the slider's root, so a selector aimed at span#root_x should aim at input#root_x, except for a slider of several values, which keeps the id on its root. A radio or checkboxes field's label has no for, which named the group's wrapper, and names the group through aria-labelledby, so a selector aimed at label[for="root_color"] should aim at #root_color__label. TitleField puts the title id on a <span> around the title's text inside its heading, so a selector or style aimed at div#root__title should aim at #root__title. FieldErrorTemplate's messages no longer carry ids of their own, so a selector aimed at #root_x__error-0 should aim at the items of #root_x__error. The theme declares @rjsf/core's RatingWidget, AltDateWidget and AltDateTimeWidget label: 'template', since none of them draws a label, so a widget of your own registered under one of those keys that draws its own label, such as a MUI Rating registered as RatingWidget or a date picker registered as AltDateWidget, should be declared label: 'self' under its key, as the "Group labels" entry above says, or it shows two labels, or, where it draws its label only while widgetDrawsLabel() is true and spreads no aria-labelledby from getControlAttributes() or getGroupAttributes(), its control is left with no name.

  • @rjsf/react-bootstrap's groups, headings, help and descriptions. RadioWidget's and CheckboxesWidget's Form.Group carries the field's id and the radiogroup or group role, named by the template's label, which FieldTemplate draws with no for, as it does for a rating or alt-date field, so a selector aimed at label[for="root_color"] should aim at label:has(#root_color__label). FieldTemplate's label puts its plan's label id on a <span> around the label's text, as core's does, so a selector aimed at label#root_color__label should aim at label #root_color__label, which matches that <span>, or at label:has(#root_color__label), which matches the label with its *. TitleField puts the title id on a <span> around the title's text, followed by a * for a required object or array, so a selector aimed at div#root__title should aim at span#root__title. TitleField draws the title it is handed rather than ui:title over it, and ArrayFieldTemplate draws only the heading ArrayField hands it as title, as core's do, so a custom field rendering either with a title of its own sees that title drawn, where the field's ui:title replaced it. FieldHelpTemplate and FieldTemplate's description render their Form.Text as a <div>, so a selector or style aimed at small#root__help should aim at div#root__help.

  • @rjsf/shadcn's range, groups, headings, help and descriptions. RangeWidget puts the field's id on its slider's thumb rather than its root, and the label names the thumb with no for. An empty range draws its thumb at its minimum, so a screen reader announces that minimum as its value, though the form holds no value until the thumb is pressed or moved. RadioWidget's and CheckboxesWidget's wrapper carries the field's id and the radiogroup or group role, named by the template's label, which FieldTemplate draws with no for, so a selector aimed at label[for="root_color"] should aim at label:has(#root_color__label). FieldTemplate's label puts its plan's label id on a <span> around the label's text, for every field, as core's does, so a selector aimed at label#root_name__label should aim at label #root_name__label, which matches that <span>, or at label:has(#root_name__label), which matches the label with its *. TitleField puts the title id on a <span> around the title's text, so a selector aimed at div#root__title should aim at span#root__title. FieldHelpTemplate and FieldTemplate's description render in a <div> rather than a <span>, so a selector or style aimed at span#root__help should aim at div#root__help.

Breaking changes: schema resolution​

@rjsf/utils now parses each root schema once into a graph of its subschemas, and retrieveSchema(), getDefaultFormState() and the form all stop a recursive $ref by one rule. A $ref is compared by the subschema it reaches, so two spellings of one target are one $ref. A field stops, with an Expand Cycle button in the form, where the first $ref it enters is already on the way down to it, or where any $ref it enters already occurs twice on that way. Every schema that overflowed the stack or ran out of memory on earlier releases now terminates. The sections below list what changes, each with the results before and after. "Before" is what 6.11.0, the last release, gives.

retrieveSchema() resolves one level at a time BREAKING CHANGE​

retrieveSchema() merges the schema's own $ref, allOf, if/then/else, dependencies and the patterns its properties match, as before. A $ref nested under properties, items or an anyOf/oneOf option is no longer resolved in place. It is handed out as written:

const rootSchema = {
  definitions: { address: { type: 'object', properties: { city: { type: 'string' } } } },
  type: 'object',
  properties: { home: { $ref: '#/definitions/address' } },
};
const retrieved = retrieveSchema(context, rootSchema, rootSchema);
// Before: retrieved.properties.home is the address definition, with its `properties`
// After: retrieved.properties.home is `{ $ref: '#/definitions/address' }`
const home = retrieveSchema(context, retrieved.properties.home, rootSchema);
// home is the address definition, with its `properties`

SchemaField and the other fields already retrieve each subschema they render, so a form renders the same. If your code reads a nested subschema out of one retrieveSchema() result, retrieve that subschema again, as the example does.

Every subschema retrieveSchema() hands out carries a Symbol-keyed property, RJSF_PROVENANCE_KEY, recording where it came from. A spread copy keeps it. It is enumerable, so toEqual() sees it: a test comparing a retrieved schema with one written by hand deletes RJSF_PROVENANCE_KEY from a copy first, or registers an equality tester that does. Retrieving such a subschema resolves it as the field it is. A recursive $ref is therefore flagged with RJSF_REF_CYCLE_KEY at the same place however many times a schema is retrieved, and retrieving a schema that retrieveSchema() returned gives it back unchanged:

const once = retrieveSchema(context, rootSchema, rootSchema, formData);
retrieveSchema(context, once, rootSchema, formData);
// Before: one more level of every recursive `$ref` is unrolled, still flagged as a cycle
// After: equal to `once`

A schema without that Symbol, such as one built in code, is resolved from the top, as before.

Expand Cycle reveals one level per click BREAKING CHANGE​

expandRefCycle() returns the schema of a flagged field resolved one level further, which CyclicSchemaField renders when its Expand Cycle button is clicked (see Option selection and cycle expansion are form state). One click now reveals one more level of the recursion, whatever the recursion goes through:

  • { type: 'object', properties: { child: { $ref: '#' } } }, after clicking #root_child_child__expand. Before: the next button is #root_child_child_child_child__expand. After: it is #root_child_child_child__expand.
  • pl = { type: 'object', properties: { a: { type: 'string' }, child: { $ref: pl } } } with a root $ref to pl, after clicking #root_child__expand. Before: the next button is #root_child_child_child__expand. After: it is #root_child_child__expand.
  • A recursion through a then or an allOf overflowed the stack or ran out of memory (below). It now reveals one level per click as well.

A few recursions now stop at a different place:

  • The first row of an array under a root $ref stops a recursive property where every other row does. With node = { properties: { name, kids: { type: 'array', items: { $ref: node } }, best: { $ref: node } } }, a root $ref to node and the data { kids: [{}] }: before, root_kids_0_best rendered and root_kids_0_best_best was collapsed. After, root_kids_0_best is collapsed, as it already was for deeper rows and under a root that is not a $ref.
  • A $ref spelled #/definitions/%41 is the same target as #/definitions/A. With A = { properties: { name, child: { $ref: '#/definitions/%41' } } } and a root $ref to A: before, root_child_child was collapsed. After, root_child is collapsed, as it is when child is written { $ref: '#/definitions/A' }.
  • A recursion through a chain of aliases stops at the first alias, since each alias is compared by the definition it reaches. With node = { type: 'object', properties: { n: { type: 'string' }, c: { $ref: A1 } } }, A1 = { $ref: A2 }, A2 = { $ref: node } and a root $ref to node: before, root_c_n rendered and root_c_c was collapsed. After, root_c is collapsed.
  • Each row of an array that the data holds renders the rows the data has below it, under any root. With node = { properties: { v, kids: { $ref: list } } }, list = { type: 'array', items: { $ref: node } }, a root that is node written out rather than a $ref to it, and the data { v: 'a', kids: [{ v: 'b', kids: [{ v: 'c', kids: [{ v: 'd' }] }] }] }: before, root_kids_0_kids was collapsed, hiding c and d. After, every row renders, down to root_kids_0_kids_0_kids_0_v, as it already did under a root $ref to node.
  • A row added to an array of a recursive definition gets the defaults the form's first row got. With A = { properties: { v, b: { $ref: B } } }, B = { type: 'array', minItems: 1, items: { $ref: A } } and a root $ref to A, after clicking #root_b__add: before, the new row was filled five levels deep, down to root_b_1_b_0_b_0_b_0_b_0_v. After, it is filled as root_b_0 is, down to root_b_1_b_0_b_0_v.

Some forms ran out of memory or overflowed the stack, and they now render with an Expand Cycle button where the recursion comes back round:

  • an allOf or a then around the recursive $ref, as in child: { allOf: [{ $ref: node }] } (#5501), or a then that declares the recursive property. Before: out of memory for the allOf, a stack overflow for the then. After: #root_child__expand.
  • an anyOf option that refers back to the schema offering it, as in node = { anyOf: [{ $ref: node }, { properties: { x } }] }. Before: out of memory. After: the selector alone, and root_x once the second option is selected.
  • definitions that all refer to one another. Four definitions, each with a $ref property to the three others: before, out of memory. After, 16 inputs and 33 Expand Cycle buttons. The size of such a form still grows factorially with the number of definitions.

Markers on resolved schemas BREAKING CHANGE​

  • resolveUiSchema() resolves a field's $ref as retrieveSchema() does, an $anchor included, so a field written { $ref: '#nd' } gets the ui:definitions entries of its definition's oneOf/anyOf options. Before, it logged could not resolve $ref in resolveUiSchema with Could not find a definition for ... and left them out.
  • A schema that merges itself back in no longer leaves a literal $ref on the result. For Pet with then: { $ref: Cat } and Cat = { allOf: [{ $ref: Pet }, ...] }: before, the merged Pet had a $ref key. After, it has none.
  • RJSF_REF_KEY and RJSF_REF_CYCLE_KEY are still added, at the places described above.
  • An extra key of the data whose additionalProperties or patternProperties $ref names a definition with an allOf keeps RJSF_REF_KEY, so it gets that definition's ui:definitions entry, as a property does. With A = { allOf: [{ type: 'object', properties: { a: { type: 'string' } } }] }, additionalProperties: { $ref: A }, the data { k: {} } and 'ui:definitions': { '#/definitions/A': { 'ui:description': 'FROM_A' } }: before, the allOf merge dropped the marker and k showed no FROM_A. After, it does, as properties: { k: { $ref: A } } already did.
  • With the default @rjsf/validator-ajv8, whose Ajv is draft-07, a $ref into a 2019-09 or 2020-12 root resolves from the first validation on. Before, the first isValid() call with such a root returned false and only later calls with the same root validated, so the first getDefaultFormState() call could take the wrong branch. With $schema 2020-12, $defs: { I: { properties: { k: { const: 'x' } } } }, properties: { k: { type: 'string', default: 'x' } }, if: { $ref: '#/$defs/I' }, then: { properties: { t: { type: 'string', default: 't' } } }, else: { properties: { e: { type: 'string', default: 'e' } } } and the data { k: 'x' }, on a fresh validator: before, the defaults were { k: 'x', e: 'e' }. After, they are { k: 'x', t: 't' }. The form rendered root_k and root_t before and after. To validate such a root under its own dialect, pass AjvClass: Ajv2020 (or Ajv2019) to customizeValidator().
  • Under a draft 2019-09 or 2020-12 root, its $schema written with or without a trailing #, a $ref to an $anchor resolves in retrieveSchema(), getDefaultFormState() and the form, as in resolveUiSchema(). Under draft-07 and earlier $anchor is no keyword, so such a $ref still throws. With a 2020-12 root whose $id is https://e.x/root, $defs: { n: { $anchor: 'nodeA', type: 'object', properties: { v: { type: 'string', default: 'v' } } } } and properties: { p: { $ref: '#nodeA' } }: before, the form and getDefaultFormState() threw Could not find a definition for https://e.x/root#nodeA.. After, the form renders root_p_v, and the defaults are { p: { v: 'v' } }.

Keywords beside a $ref BREAKING CHANGE​

A $ref with keywords beside it is read as JSON Schema reads it, under every draft, in the form, the defaults, option scoring and omitExtraData(): as the allOf of those keywords and of the schema the $ref names. Before, the keywords beside a field's own $ref overrode the schema it names keyword by keyword under every draft, and under draft-07 and earlier a $ref reached through another $ref dropped the keywords beside it. With Pet = { type: 'object', properties: { name: { type: 'string', default: 'n' } }, required: ['name'] } and cat: { $ref: Pet, properties: { meow: { type: 'string', default: 'm' } } }:

  • the form renders root_cat_meow beside root_cat_name, where it rendered root_cat_meow alone, and Pet's required applies to cat;
  • the defaults are { cat: { meow: 'm', name: 'n' } }, where they were { cat: { meow: 'm' } }. The keywords beside a $ref are no allOf the schema declares, so they are filled whatever the allOf defaults behavior;
  • omitExtraData(), which the omitExtraData and liveOmit props run, keeps { cat: { name: 'x', meow: 'y' } } of the data { cat: { name: 'x', meow: 'y', z: 1 } }, where it kept { cat: { meow: 'y' } }.

The same holds where another $ref reaches such a $ref, as v: { $ref: M } reaches M = { $ref: O, properties: { b: { type: 'string', default: 'b' } } } with O = { properties: { a: { type: 'string', default: 'a' } } }. Under draft-07 the form renders root_v_b beside root_v_a, where it rendered root_v_a alone, and the defaults are { v: { b: 'b', a: 'a' } }, where they were { v: { a: 'a' } }. With the options [{ type: 'object', properties: { a: { type: 'string' } } }, { $ref: M }] and no selected option, getClosestMatchingOption() picks the second option for { b: 'y' }, where with @rjsf/validator-ajv8 and @rjsf/validator-cfworker it matched no option and returned the selected option, -1 (@rjsf/validator-ata already picked the second); it picks the first for { a: 'y' }, as before. The keywords beside the $ref come first in the merge, so a field renders them first, and where both sides declare an annotation, theirs wins. A customMergeAllOf merges the two as it merges an allOf, in the form, the defaults, option scoring and omitExtraData() alike.

Annotations are read as before: a $ref whose only other keywords are title, description, default, examples, readOnly, writeOnly, deprecated, $comment, $id, $anchor, $defs, definitions and $schema reads as the schema it names, with the annotations beside it over its own. So { $ref: Status, default: 'active' } defaults to 'active' whatever Status declares, and a $ref beside nothing but $defs fills its target's defaults: with $defs: { a: { $defs: { n: { type: 'number', default: 7 } }, $ref: '#/$defs/a/$defs/n' } } and properties: { l: { $ref: '#/$defs/a' } }, the defaults are { l: 7 } where they were {}.

A dependencies entry is qualified by the properties of the schema that declares it, as before, so one in the schema a $ref names is not qualified by the properties beside the $ref, and one beside a $ref with no properties beside it is qualified by any key the data holds.

getDefaultFormState() folds over the schema graph BREAKING CHANGE​

getDefaultFormState() reads the same schema graph as retrieveSchema(). Each field's schema is merged from its $ref, its allOf (under allOf: 'populateDefaults', or where the field has an if), its then/else and its dependencies, as the form renders the field. A recursive $ref stops where the form shows an Expand Cycle button. Its defaults are filled one level further, once, as if that button had been clicked. The dependencies are applied again until the defaults bring no new key that qualifies another one.
