Check a record's widget entries, such as text, email, checkbox and select, which now span properties that don't name that widget too, and change or remove each one where that isn't wanted.

A custom field that builds its ObjectFieldTemplate's properties itself sets each one's renderedAs with createSchemaFieldRenderedAs() from @rjsf/core, handing it what it hands the property's SchemaField. Without renderedAs, antd keys a property by nothing, so it gets the default span:

+import { createSchemaFieldRenderedAs } from '@rjsf/core';
+
   return {
     content: <SchemaField name={name} schema={propertySchema} uiSchema={propertyUiSchema} formData={propertyData} fieldPath={propertyPath} {...rest} />,
     name,
     hidden,
+    renderedAs: () => createSchemaFieldRenderedAs()(propertySchema, propertyUiSchema, propertyData, propertyPath, registry),
   };

See renderedAs for keeping one per property across renders.

@rjsf/antd and @rjsf/mantine leave out a property hidden by deprecatedHandling or ui:definitions BREAKING CHANGE​

ObjectField marks a property hidden for its ObjectFieldTemplate whenever the property's field renders hidden, not only for the property's own ui:widget: 'hidden': also for a deprecated property under deprecatedHandling: 'hide', and for a ui:widget: 'hidden' the property's ui:definitions entry sets (#5507). The antd and mantine ObjectFieldTemplates leave out every hidden property. Before: such a property's field rendered inside its theme's hidden wrapper (antd's rjsf-field-hidden div, mantine's display: none Box), in a column or grid cell of its own. After: it doesn't render, and the other properties share the row as they do beside a property with its own ui:widget: 'hidden'. The property's value stays in the form data, but its input is no longer in the DOM, so a native submit or new FormData(form) no longer posts it. A test that looked the input up reads the value from the form instead:

- expect(container.querySelector('#root_b')).toHaveValue('legacy');
+ expect(formRef.current?.getFormData()).toMatchObject({ b: 'legacy' });

A $ref cycle whose field renders hidden has no Expand button BREAKING CHANGE​

CyclicSchemaField renders nothing in place of its Expand button for a $ref cycle whose field one level further renders hidden, since expanding it would show nothing, and ObjectField marks such a property hidden, expanded or not (#5507). That is a cycle whose own uiSchema or ui:definitions entry sets ui:widget: 'hidden', or, under deprecatedHandling: 'hide', one that is deprecated beside its $ref or where the $ref leads. With this schema and uiSchema: { child: { 'ui:widget': 'hidden' } }, before, #root_child__expand rendered, and clicking it rendered a hidden field. After, neither renders.

{
  "definitions": {
    "node": { "type": "object", "properties": { "child": { "$ref": "#/definitions/node" } } }
  },
  "$ref": "#/definitions/node"
}

A test that clicked the button to reach that field reads the field's value from the form data instead.

An array item's handlers do only what its buttons can BREAKING CHANGE​

onAddClick, onAddItem, onCopyItem, onRemoveItem, onMoveUpItem and onMoveDownItem now do nothing where the button can't act, whatever the template draws (#5677). That covers the first item up, the last item down, moving or removing a fixed tuple item, adding after or copying one that isn't the last, adding to an optional array without data, whose data its optionalDataControl starts, a disabled or read-only array or item (an item's own lock leaves onAddItem, as it leaves the add button), and an option or limit that takes the button away, such as ui:orderable: false, ui:removable: false, ui:copyable left off or maxItems. maxItems and the last item are checked against the items at the call, so a template can call onRemoveItem() and then onAddItem() in one handler at the limit, or onAddItem() and then onMoveDownItem() on the last item, and a second onAddItem() past the limit does nothing. buttonsProps.canAdd tells whether onAddItem acts: it is false on a disabled or read-only array, and after a tuple's fixed item that isn't the last, even where the array's add button shows. The array's own canAdd still tells only that the array is addable and has room, since the add button shows, disabled, on a disabled or read-only array. An ArrayFieldTemplate that renders its own add button has to disable it on disabled || readonly itself, as the built-in ones do, or the button does nothing when pressed. An ArrayFieldItemButtonsTemplate that renders its own buttons likewise shows each only under its hasMoveUp, hasMoveDown, hasCopy or hasRemove and disables it on disabled || readonly, or a button that can't act stays on screen and does nothing, where Remove on a disabled or read-only array used to remove the item. A refused call still prevents the event's default, so a button that isn't type='button' doesn't submit the form.

A template that hides core's arrows with ui:orderable: false and reorders through these handlers, as a drag-and-drop template does, now gets no move. Leave ui:orderable on and leave the arrows out of your own ArrayFieldItemButtonsTemplate instead:

- uiSchema = { 'ui:orderable': false };
+ templates = { ArrayFieldItemButtonsTemplate: MyButtonsWithoutArrows };

Copy shows only from a tuple's last fixed item on BREAKING CHANGE​

In an array with fixed items and additionalItems, core's Copy button no longer shows on a fixed item before the last (#5677). A copy goes below its item, so a copy of an earlier fixed item pushed the fixed items after it into positions of another schema. Copy shows on the last fixed item and on the additional items after it.

A fixed item before the last whose only button was Copy now has none, so its hasToolbar is false and templates drop its toolbar, which changes its layout: core's leaves out the rjsf-array-item-toolbox element, and @rjsf/bootstrap3's widens its content from col-xs-9 col-md-10 col-xl-11 to col-xs-12, so its inputs no longer line up with those of the items that keep buttons. Snapshots and CSS that relied on that toolbar change with it.

Under itemLabel, items are named only when they have buttons, and a fixed item before the last, which can't be moved or removed, now has none, so the numbers that tell items of one name apart no longer count it. In a tuple of two fixed items with an additional one, all three named x, the Copy buttons were Copy x (1), Copy x (2) and Copy x (3), and are now Copy x (1) on the last fixed item and Copy x (2) on the additional one, whose Remove button is Remove x (2) too.

A test that finds a fixed item's Copy button, or a button by one of those numbered titles, finds it on the item that still shows it, by its new number.

A disabled or read-only array item disables its own buttons BREAKING CHANGE​

An array item that is disabled or read-only on its own, not through the array, now has its move, copy and remove buttons disabled too, the way its inputs are (#2504). That is an item made so by the items or additionalItems uiSchema (ui:disabled or ui:readonly, static or from the items function), a ui:definitions entry for the items' $ref, or a readOnly in the item's own schema. A readOnly on its selected anyOf/oneOf option locks only the inputs. Before, only the inputs were locked, and the item could still be moved, copied and removed. A deprecated item that deprecatedHandling: 'disable' disables keeps its buttons, so it can still be removed. An item's own ui:disabled: false or ui:readonly: false under a disabled or read-only array, or form, still enables only its inputs, and the buttons stay disabled. ArrayFieldItemTemplate's disabled and readonly are the same as its buttons', so they are now true for such an item too, where they used to be only the array's.

The add button stays enabled, and the row it adds is locked as soon as it appears. That works when the items have a default. Without one the row can't be filled or removed and it fails validation, so set 'ui:options': { addable: false } on the array.

To keep an object item's rows movable and removable while its values stay read-only, put readOnly on its properties instead of on the item:

 items: {
   type: 'object',
-  readOnly: true,
-  properties: { name: { type: 'string' } },
+  properties: { name: { type: 'string', readOnly: true } },
 },

Move a ui:readonly or ui:disabled from items onto its properties the same way, as items: { name: { 'ui:readonly': true } }. The item's lock reached every property, its additionalProperties and any nested array's buttons, so give each of them its own readOnly or ui:readonly to keep them locked; a property left without one becomes editable, and a nested array's add, move and remove buttons become enabled. The add button of an item with additionalProperties becomes enabled too, and no property's readOnly locks it, so remove it with 'ui:options': { expandable: false } on items.

A list of plain values, such as items: { type: 'string', readOnly: true } or items: { 'ui:readonly': true } on a list of strings, has no properties to move the lock onto, and ui:readonly: false on the items unlocks their inputs too. The same goes for ui:disabled on such a list. There is no setting that keeps such rows movable and removable while their values stay read-only or disabled. Render the buttons with a custom ArrayFieldItemButtonsTemplate that leaves out readonly, or disabled for ui:disabled, keeping in mind that it then also enables them in a read-only or disabled array or form.

sanitizeDataForNewSchema() removes the keys it discards, and leaves out objects the data doesn't hold BREAKING CHANGE​

This affects code that calls sanitizeDataForNewSchema(), or schemaUtils.sanitizeDataForNewSchema(), and reads what it returns. Form and its anyOf/oneOf switch already handle the new shape.

These placeholders it used to write are gone, at every level of the data:

  • A key the old schema declares and the new one doesn't, or declares with another type, is removed. Before, it was kept holding undefined.
  • An object property the data doesn't hold, or holds as null where neither its type list nor nullable: true allows null, is left out. Before, it was written as {} wherever its schema declares properties, and a null was kept where it declares none.
  • A key the new schema still declares but whose value it rejects, through its const, its enum, a readOnly default or a prefix item the array can't hold, is removed, so the defaults fill it in. An array keeps the items past its prefix that its new items allow, and drops the rest. A key the data already holds as undefined keeps it where the old schema declares the same type, const, enum or constant options, maxItems and default for it, the default the object declares for it included, and is otherwise removed too unless a value replaces it, as a top-level clear is when anyOf/oneOf options are switched. Before, it was set to undefined, which kept the defaults from reaching it.

With old = { type: 'object', properties: { x: { type: 'object', properties: { p: { type: 'string' } } } } }, newSchema the same with q in place of p, and the data { x: { p: 'v' } }:

-{ x: { p: undefined } }
+{ x: {} }

With newSchema = { type: 'object', properties: { k: { type: 'string' }, opt: { type: 'object', properties: { x: { type: 'string' } } } } } and the data { k: 'a' }:

-{ k: 'a', opt: {} }
+{ k: 'a' }

If you spread the result over the old data to clear what it discarded, the spread no longer clears those keys. Use the result on its own instead:

-const next = { ...oldData, ...schemaUtils.sanitizeDataForNewSchema(newSchema, oldSchema, oldData) };
+const next = schemaUtils.sanitizeDataForNewSchema(newSchema, oldSchema, oldData);

If you need the objects for a schema's optional object properties, fill them in with getDefaultFormState(), as a mount does. In a test that asserts the result, drop the undefined keys and the {} placeholders from the expected value. toEqual() already treats a key holding undefined as absent, but it doesn't ignore a {}.

New Features​

getFormData() and the FormRef type​

The form owns its data, the way an <input> with a defaultValue does (see Form owns its data), and until now the only way to see it was onChange, so autosave, an "unsaved changes" guard, or a submit button rendered outside the form all had to copy every change into your own state. getFormData() reads it on demand:

function Editor({ record }) {
  const formRef = useRef<FormRef>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setInterval(() => api.draft(formRef.current?.getFormData()), 30_000);
    return () => clearInterval(timer);
  }, []);

  return <Form ref={formRef} schema={schema} validator={validator} initialFormData={record} />;
}

It returns the form's current value: the seed, filled in with the schema's defaults, and every edit made since, including one React has yet to show in the inputs.

FormRef<T> names every supported ref member. The ref section above shows how to type a ref against it.

transformChange​

A pure (next, previous) => data prop that decides what an edit leaves the form with: next takes the edit, previous refuses it, and any other value rewrites it, before the form stores, validates and reports the result. It replaces refusing an edit by not storing it, which no longer works now that the form owns its data. See Refuse or rewrite an edit in transformChange.

ui:initialValue and ui:required​

Two new uiSchema directives complement the extended ui:emptyValue above, for forms that want to control a field's initial value or required-ness without editing the underlying schema:

  • ui:initialValue pre-fills a field on initial render and after a form reset. It takes priority over schema.default, but never overrides formData that's already been provided. This is useful for a field — often hidden — that a particular form wants to fix to a known value, e.g. a country field defaulted to 'US' for a US-only form.
  • ui:required overrides a field's required status from the UI side only. Setting it to true shows the required indicator and adds the field to the effective required set used for validation, even if the schema doesn't mark it required. Setting it to false hides the indicator on a schema-required field, but does not suppress schema-level validation — pair it with ui:initialValue or ui:emptyValue so the field always has a value, or you'll get a console.warn. ui:required must be set per field; it is not honored via ui:globalOptions.

See ui:initialValue and ui:required for details and examples.

ui:required is enforced by walking the rendered form itself rather than by rewriting the schema handed to your validator, so it works the same way regardless of which validator you use — including the precompiled validators (AJV8PrecompiledValidator from @rjsf/validator-ajv8 and ATAPrecompiledValidator from @rjsf/validator-ata), which enforce it too. The one difference from a schema-level required error: a ui:required error is built by RJSF, not your validator, so it doesn't pass through a custom transformErrors function and doesn't carry validator-specific fields like AJV's params.missingProperty. See ui:required for details.

ui:options.optgroups for grouped <select> options​

Every theme's SelectWidget now supports grouping enum options into labeled sections (rendered as <optgroup> elements, or each theme's closest equivalent — see the optgroups docs for the specifics per theme) via ui:options.optgroups:

const uiSchema: UiSchema = {
  'ui:options': {
    optgroups: {
      Latin: ['lorem', 'ipsum', 'dolorem'],
      Greek: ['alpha', 'beta', 'gamma'],
    },
  },
};

Keys are the group labels; values are arrays of enum values belonging to that group. Enum values not listed in any group render ungrouped after the groups. This is purely additive — existing forms are unaffected unless optgroups is set.

propertyNames.enum renders the key as a dropdown​

An object whose propertyNames enumerates the allowed key names now renders each additionalProperties/patternProperties key as a dropdown of those names rather than a free-text input, in every theme:

const schema: RJSFSchema = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: { type: 'boolean' },
  propertyNames: { enum: ['darkMode', 'betaBanner', 'offlineCache'] },
};

A name another key already holds is left out of the dropdown, and the add button creates the new property under the first allowed name that is still free instead of newKey. registry.schemaUtils.canExpand() hides the add button once every allowed name is taken, the way it already does at the maxProperties limit, so a custom ObjectFieldTemplate that calls it picks this up on its own. A propertyNames without an enum, such as one constraining names by pattern, keeps the free-text input, so existing forms are unaffected.

The names reach WrapIfAdditionalTemplate as a new optional propertyNamesEnum prop on FieldTemplateProps/WrapIfAdditionalTemplateProps. A custom FieldTemplate that lists the props it forwards to WrapIfAdditionalTemplate one by one, rather than spreading them, has to add propertyNamesEnum to that list for the dropdown to appear, and keyName for the key it renders to be the real one (see FieldTemplateProps gains a required keyName). A custom WrapIfAdditionalTemplate renders the dropdown by handing the prop to the new AdditionalPropertyKeySelect component from @rjsf/utils, which resolves the theme's own SelectWidget:

{propertyNamesEnum ? (
  <AdditionalPropertyKeySelect
    id={additionalKeyId(id)}
    label={keyLabel}
    value={keyName}
    propertyNamesEnum={propertyNamesEnum}
    onKeyRename={onKeyRename}
    disabled={disabled}
    readonly={readonly}
    required={required}
    registry={registry}
  />
) : (
  <input type='text' id={additionalKeyId(id)} onBlur={onKeyRenameBlur} defaultValue={keyName} />
)}

Multiple types and unconstrained properties can be edited through the fallback UI​

JSON Schema lets a type be a list of types. v6 rendered the first type in that list and gave no way to reach the others, and it rendered a property described only by additionalProperties: true as a field for whatever type the data happened to hold, with the same one-way door. Turning on the useFallbackUiForUnsupportedType prop now renders both through FallbackField, which pairs a type selector with the field for the type currently chosen:

const schema: RJSFSchema = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    // a selector offering exactly these three types
    multi: { type: ['string', 'number', 'boolean'] },
    // a selector offering every JSON Schema type, for each key added here
    anything: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true },
  },
};

render(<Form schema={schema} validator={validator} useFallbackUiForUnsupportedType />, document.getElementById('app'));

Switching the type casts the value that is already there where it can (a number to its string spelling, a string to the number it reads as) and starts from an empty value where it cannot, such as an object, an array, or a number from text that reads as no number at all. The selector also now offers integer and null alongside the five types it offered in v6, and starts on the type the current form data has. Every other keyword of the schema still describes the value, so a union declaring properties, items, format or minimum keeps them for whichever type is in effect.

A schema pairing multiple types with an anyOf or oneOf whose options name no type gets both selectors: the type selector wraps the option selector, and each option renders for whichever type is currently chosen. Every member of the union is therefore reachable from within an option, where in v6 an option could only ever be the first type in the list. A list with an option naming a type of its own gets no selector around it, and any option in it naming no type renders a type selector of its own, unless the list mixes the two on a schema whose first type is object, or names only its own types on such a schema whose ui:field or $id names the fallback field.

Four things are deliberately unchanged:

  • A nullable type (['string', 'null']) still renders as a plain string field, since getSchemaType() resolves it to that single type. Only a union of more than one non-null type gets a selector.
  • With the prop off (the default), there is still no selector, since it is the opt-in fallback UI, so a union renders one field for one of its types. That is the first type in the list that JSON Schema defines other than null, so ['null', 'string', 'number'] renders its string and ['foo', 'string'] its string rather than the unsupported-field box. A ui:widget that only another listed string, number, integer or boolean type has renders that type's field instead, so a textarea on a ['number', 'string'] renders StringField where v6 threw; a format picks no other type's field. A union paired with an anyOf or oneOf stays one-way too, since the option selector alone cannot reach the other types.
  • A schema pinning its value with an enum, a const, or an anyOf/oneOf of constants renders as the select or constant field it always has, with no type selector, since switching type would only cast a value the user picked into one the schema rejects.
  • A field whose ui:widget is a component renders through that control alone, with no type selector, the same way one with a ui:field does. A control written for that schema handles the types it allows, so wrapping it would pin the schema to one of them and cast the value on every switch. A ui:widget naming a widget by string is a theme's control for a single type, which is the choice the selector is there to make, so it renders within the selector instead — and is dropped for a chosen type the theme has no implementation of. A schema with no usable type of its own — an unrecognized type, or an additionalProperties entry left unconstrained — still gets a selector, since it lists no types for such a control to handle, and the widget renders within it for whichever type is chosen. A list naming an unrecognized type alongside a recognized one offers only the recognized ones, null included: a ['foo', 'null'] offers null and nothing else.

See Multiple types for details.

additionalPropertiesWhenAbsent reads an object naming no additionalProperties as the spec does​

JSON Schema reads an object that names neither additionalProperties nor unevaluatedProperties as taking any extra key, as additionalProperties: true does, where the form has always read it as taking none (#2137). The new additionalPropertiesWhenAbsent prop, 'forbid' by default, has the form follow the spec when set to 'allow': such an object gets an add button, the extra keys of its data render with their key input, and omitExtraData keeps them. An object anyOf/oneOf union then renders its own title and add button beside the option it shows; give it additionalProperties: false to keep it closed. See Objects naming no additionalProperties.

Utilities no other RJSF package uses are no longer exported from @rjsf/utils BREAKING CHANGE​

This affects code that imports one of the 6.x exports below from @rjsf/utils, which now exports only what another RJSF package uses. The ones RJSF still needs are unchanged, just no longer exported; the rest are deleted.

ExportUse instead
canExpand()registry.schemaUtils.canExpand(schema, uiSchema, formData)
ariaDescribedByIds()getControlDescribedBy({ id, presentation }), or widgetAriaProps() for a widget; for ariaDescribedByIds(id, true), which also named the examples list, pass [examplesId(id)] as getControlDescribedBy()'s second argument
dataURItoBlob()useFileWidgetProps() in a file widget, which gives each file's name, size and type; elsewhere, split the URL at ;base64,: the part before holds the type up to its first ; and the file name in a URI-encoded name= parameter, and new Blob([Uint8Array.from(atob(base64), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0))], { type }) builds the blob. fetch(dataURL) keeps the name= parameter in the blob's type and is blocked by a connect-src policy that doesn't allow data:
dateRangeOptions(), getDateElementProps(), parseDateString(), toDateString(), pad()useAltDateWidgetProps() and DateElement, which build the date parts; outside a widget, the UTC getters of new Date(value) for parseDateString(), adding 1 to getUTCMonth() for its 1-based month (it gave -1 for every part of an empty value, threw Unable to parse date <value> for a string new Date() can't parse, where the getters give NaN, and gave 0 for the hour, minute and second when includeTime was false, where the getters give the parsed ones), new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day, hour, minute, second)).toJSON() for toDateString(), followed by .slice(0, 10) for toDateString(date, false), and String(value).padStart(width, '0') for pad()
findSchemaDefinition()registry.schemaUtils.retrieveSchema({ $ref }) in a field or widget. Without a registry, or for a $ref into another root, retrieveSchema({ validator }, { $ref }, rootSchema). Both need a validator, and both resolve more than the definition: an allOf in it is merged and its if/then/else and dependencies are resolved against no data, and the result carries RJSF's Symbol markers. A $ref inside the definition is left as it is, and a $ref the root doesn't define throws, as before.
getInputProps()getBaseInputProps(), which takes a BaseInputTemplate's props: outside a template, pass it { schema, type, options, registry }, where registry needs only translateString, and pass getInputProps()'s fourth argument as its second, plainNativeInput, which also decides whether a number/integer field gets a text input with a numeric inputMode and pattern. It returns more than getInputProps() did: a title naming that numeric pattern, an accept, inputMode or pattern passed in its props in place of the derived one, and multiple set to undefined for any input but a file input, so it overrides a multiple spread before it, such as on an email input
getTemplate()getTemplates(registry, uiOptions), destructuring the template you need. It resolves only the names the registry holds: an override in ui:options under a name the registry has no template for, which getTemplate() returned, is left out, so read such a template from uiOptions yourself and name its props with isComponentType<P>()
getWidget()resolveWidget(schema, widget, registry.widgets), destructuring its Widget
hashForSchema()hashObject(), which hashes the schema the same way
hashString(), sortedJSONStringify()Nothing: copy their 6.x implementation. hashObject(x) is hashString(sortedJSONStringify(x)), so it neither returns the JSON nor hashes a string as hashString() did: hashObject('abc') hashes "abc", quotes included
mergeDefaultsWithFormData()getDefaultFormState(), or mergeObjects() for plain objects, which replaces an array where mergeDefaultsWithFormData() merged its items and has nothing in place of its mergeExtraArrayDefaults, defaultSupercedesUndefined and overrideFormDataWithDefaults arguments, so an undefined value always overwrites its default
replaceStringParameters()englishStringTranslator() for a TranslatableString; for a string of your own, replace %1, %2, … yourself
schemaParser()getValidationSchemas()
withIdRefPrefix()withRootIdRefPrefix(schema, {}), which prefixes a local # $ref with ROOT_SCHEMA_PREFIX and leaves a relative one as written, as 6.x did. Passing the real root instead gives a root with an $id that $id as the prefix, resolves relative $refs against it and re-spells those inside a nested $id, so a validator holding the root under ROOT_SCHEMA_PREFIX can't resolve them. Unlike 6.x, it takes only a schema object, not an array or a primitive
DEFINITIONS_KEY, DEPENDENCIES_KEY, ENUM_KEY, IF_KEY, DISCRIMINATOR_PATH, FORM_CONTEXT_NAMEThe string or path they hold: 'definitions', 'dependencies', 'enum', 'if', ['discriminator', 'propertyName'], 'formContext'
isValueEmpty(), NAME_KEY, RJSF_PREFIX_KEYNothing: they served RJSF's own code

New types​

The following new types were added to @rjsf/utils:

  • AdditionalPropertyKeySelectProps<T, S, F>: the props of the AdditionalPropertyKeySelect component.
  • ArrayFieldItemButtonProps: the props ArrayFieldItemButtonsTemplateProps.itemButtonProps hands each of an array item's copy, moveDown, moveUp and remove buttons, holding a key only for the buttons the item can show.
  • Bivariant<Args, R>: a callback whose parameters are checked bivariantly, the way React checks event handlers, so an implementation may declare narrower parameters than the callback's own. SlotComponent and the onChange props are built from it, and the CompiledValidateFunction of @rjsf/validator-ajv8 and of @rjsf/validator-ata extends it.
  • ClassMap: the class names a theme or a form gives the elements @rjsf/core renders, one key per element. See Registry has a required classMap.
  • CoreUiOptionsChecks (@rjsf/core): The UiOptionsCheck union describing @rjsf/core's own built-in widgets, fields and ui:options. Pass it as StrictUiSchema's Checks argument (union it with your own Checks to extend it further) - it isn't included automatically.
  • CustomTemplateEntries: the part of TemplatesType holding custom templates, alone or in named groups, under its string index signature. See The templates prop of Form and withTheme() checks declared templates.
  • DateTimeLocalValueResult: what getDateTimeLocalValue() returns: isIsoDateTime, requiresOffset and the localValue a datetime-local input displays.
  • DeclaredTemplatesType<T, S, F>: the part of TemplatesType holding the templates RJSF declares, each typed with its own props, without the index signature for custom ones. See The templates prop of Form and withTheme() checks declared templates.
  • EventFormData<T> (@rjsf/core): the type of IChangeEvent.formData and FormRef.getFormData(). See Generic defaults are unknown instead of any.
  • FieldPath: a branded string identifying a field by the path to its data, such as friends[0].firstName. See Field identity.
  • FormClassMap: the classMap a Form takes, a ClassMap whose entries may also be a function of the class beneath, so a form can extend that class rather than repeat it. See Registry has a required classMap.
  • FormFieldState<S>: what a form shows beyond its schema and data, which getDefaultFormState(), getUiRequiredErrorSchema() and omitExtraData() take as an optional fieldState: selectedOption(), the option each field shows, isExpanded(), whether the user expanded a collapsed $ref cycle, the optional drawsControlsBesideOptions(), whether an object draws its Optional Data Controls beside its anyOf/oneOf options, the optional fallbackType(), the type the fallback UI's type selector is on for a field it renders, and the optional rendersArrayWidget(), whether ArrayField renders a field as one widget. getDefaultFormState() computes a field's defaults from the option it shows, and the other two walk the fields on screen. Form passes its own. See FormFieldState.
  • GetDefaultFormStateProps<T, S, F>: the props object getDefaultFormState() takes after the SchemaContext.
  • GlobalUISchemaOptionsExtensions<E, Reserved>: checks the keys an extension of GlobalUISchemaOptions adds, mapping each one RJSF reserves, or a string index signature, to never. See ui:globalOptions hold only the options RJSF reads there.
  • GlobalUISchemaOptionsKeys: the options RJSF reads from ui:globalOptions, as fallbacks for a field that sets none of its own. See ui:globalOptions hold only the options RJSF reads there.
  • GroupRole: 'radiogroup' | 'group', the role getGroupAttributes() gives the element wrapping a group of controls.
  • IndexedEnumOptionType<S>, EnumOptionsGroupType<S>, GroupedEnumOptionsType<S>: the option/group shapes returned by groupEnumOptions().
  • LogOnceLevel: 'warn' | 'error', the console method logOnce() logs through.
  • MarkdownTemplateProps<T, S, F>: the props a MarkdownTemplate receives, generic over the same <T, S, F> as every other template's props. children is the markdown string to render; uiSchema and registry are picked from the form's base props, so an implementation can read ui:options, reach registry.translateString, or fall back to another template.
  • MergedClassMap: a form's ClassMap once buildRegistry() layered the Form's over the theme's over @rjsf/core's, holding every key, undefined where no layer gives the element a class. See Registry has a required classMap.
  • PartialTemplatesType<T, S, F>: any subset of the templates, as the templates prop of Form, a theme's templates and getTestRegistry() take: each declared template, each button of ButtonTemplates on its own, and custom entries. See The templates prop of Form and withTheme() checks declared templates.
  • PresentationDeclaration, ThemePresentation, FieldPresentation: the presentation metadata proposed in #5490, which @rjsf/core and every theme read. A PresentationDeclaration names who draws each part of a field (a PresentationPart: its label, description, errors and help) as a PartOwner: 'template', 'self' or, for a field that renders a single widget, 'widget', plus labelledBy, whether a label the template draws reaches the control through its for or through the control's aria-labelledby. A widget's declarations, a ThemePresentation's widgets and default, are WidgetPresentationDeclarations, which can't name the 'widget' owner; its default and fieldDefault take no uncheckedIsFalse, which is declared under the key of the one widget it describes. A ThemePresentation holds declarations by registry key under widgets and fields, plus default for the parts of every widget that the layer's own entry for it doesn't declare, custom and unregistered widgets included, and fieldDefault for the parts of every field that its merged entry doesn't declare, custom fields included, which is also what a part a field leaves to its widget falls back to when it renders none; mergeThemePresentation() merges a form's layers into a MergedThemePresentation. A FieldPresentation is one field's resolved plan: each part as a PartPresentation, placed 'template', 'self', 'above' (drawn by a field above rendering the same id) or 'none' (a PartPlacement) under the id it renders with, the describedBy ids of its parts that render, which a field below rendering the same id inherits, the showLabel its ui:label resolved to, its label's requiredMarker, planned for a container's heading too and carried by an above label from the label drawn above, its control's ControlAttributes, and the inherited plan of the field above rendering the same id. ResolvedPresentationDeclaration is what getPresentationDeclaration() returns, with every part settled on 'template' or 'self'. Nothing is declared on a component: one given directly, as a ui:field or ui:widget, takes the declaration for the first key it is registered under that declares it.
  • PresentationSource<T, S, F>, PresentationSubject<T, S, F>, FieldPresentationInputs, FieldLabelSources<S>: the parameter types of getPresentationDeclaration(), resolveFieldPresentation() and getFieldLabel().
  • RawValidationResult<E>: what ValidatorType.rawValidation() returns: the engine's errors, typed E, and the validationError thrown when validation couldn't run. See any members of the public types are specific types.
  • ReservedUiOptionName: the names an extension of GlobalUISchemaOptions may not reuse: every option name RJSF reads for a field, and definitions and globalOptions, which only the root uiSchema's ui: keys set. See ui:globalOptions hold only the options RJSF reads there.
  • SchemaContext<S, F>: the validator, customMergeAllOf, defaultFormStateBehavior and additionalPropertiesWhenAbsent every validator-based schema function takes as its first parameter. See @rjsf/utils schema functions take a SchemaContext in place of the validator.
  • SchemaFlagMarker: the flag markers hasSchemaMarker() reads, ADDITIONAL_PROPERTY_FLAG, GUESSED_TYPE_FLAG and RJSF_REF_CYCLE_KEY, for a function that wraps it.
  • SlotComponent<P>: the component-slot type behind Widget, Field and every TemplatesType entry: a function or class component taking P, with its props checked bivariantly. See Widget type.
  • StrictUiSchema<Checks, T, S, F>: the opt-in form of UiSchema that narrows ui:widget/ui:field/ui:options to a Checks union's vocabulary. See Type-safe UiSchema (opt-in).
  • ThemedForm<T, S, F> (@rjsf/core): what withTheme() returns. See withTheme() returns a ThemedForm.
  • ThemeGlobalUISchemaOptions<ThemeExtensions, UserExtensions>: the ui:globalOptions of a theme that reads options of its own, whose extensions may not reuse an option name RJSF reads, and a user's may not reuse the theme's either. See ui:globalOptions hold only the options RJSF reads there.
  • UiOptionsCheck: The { when, then } shape a Checks union is built from, each rule declaring the widget/field/option vocabulary StrictUiSchema allows for a given form-data type.
  • UseOptionFocusHandlersResult: what useOptionFocusHandlers() returns: the focusHandlers and blurHandlers of each option, by position.
  • UseSelectFocusHandlersResult: what useSelectFocusHandlers() returns: its handleFocus and handleBlur.
  • UseTimeWidgetPropsResult: what useTimeWidgetProps() returns: isIsoTime, the localValue a time input displays, and computeTimeValue().
  • VisibleErrorsProps: the parameter type of hasVisibleErrors(), deprecated with it. See A field's label, description, help and errors are drawn where its plan says.
  • WidgetAliasFor<Type>: the ui:widget alias names resolveWidget() accepts for a JSON Schema type, such as 'text' | 'textarea' | 'password' | ... for WidgetAliasFor<'string'>.
  • WidgetAriaPropsInput<T, S, F>: the props widgetAriaProps() builds a SelectWidget's accessible name and description from.

Type-safe UiSchema (opt-in)​

StrictUiSchema<Checks, T, S, F> is a new, opt-in form of UiSchema: pass it a Checks union and it narrows ui:widget/ui:field/ui:options to only the values valid for each field's form-data type. An inline uiSchema JSX literal gets this narrowing too, by checking it with TypeScript's satisfies operator - no wrapper component needed.

UiSchema is otherwise unchanged - using StrictUiSchema is entirely opt-in and can be done incrementally, field by field or form by form.

See Type-safe UiSchema for the full documentation, including examples, how to extend the widget/option vocabulary via Checks, and the current known gaps.

@rjsf/utils also exports new constants, all described in Constants in the API reference, among them WIDGET_FIELD_PRESENTATION and DEFAULT_BOOLEAN_WIDGET (#5456), and JSON_SCHEMA_TYPES, every JSON Schema type name in the order the fallback UI offers them (#5323).

Changes to existing utility functions​

  • Every validator-based schema function: Takes a SchemaContext in place of its validator, and no longer takes a customMergeAllOf or defaultFormStateBehavior. See @rjsf/utils schema functions take a SchemaContext in place of the validator
  • enumOptionSelectedValue(): In the realValue format the selected value is encoded the same way enumOptionsDomValues() encodes the options' values, instead of with String(), so a selected object or null value now matches its option. It also no longer reports "no selection" purely because the value equals the emptyValue a widget passed it, so an option carrying that widget's null or '' sentinel shows as selected. An entry of a multiple selection that matches no option is left out, as the indexed format leaves it out
  • enumOptionsIsSelected(): Takes an optional third multiple argument. A single-select widget passes false, so an array selected is compared as the whole value of an array option such as { "const": [2] } rather than as a list of selections; omitted, an array is still a list. enumOptionsIndexForValue() prefers an option matching the whole value when not multiple, which fixes enumOptionSelectedValue() for array constants too, and the radio widgets pass false
  • enumOptionsSelectValue(): Compares values by deep equality and accepts a null option, so an object option selected in a checkbox list lands in the options' order, whether or not the form data holds the option's own instance It no longer adds a value that is already selected, and keeps a selected value that matches no option after the ones that do
  • enumOptionValueDecoder(): In the realValue format a string decodes to the option enumOptionsDomValues() encodes as that string, and no longer falls back to the option at a bare index no option encodes as. That fallback returned the wrong option whenever a number option shared its value with another option's position, e.g. '1' decoded to 1 rather than 5 for the options 1 and 5. A widget that holds an option's position resolves it with enumOptionsValueForIndex() instead.
  • getDefaultFormState(): Takes a SchemaContext followed by a GetDefaultFormStateProps object, and added optional uiSchema and uiSchemaDefinitions props used to apply ui:emptyValue and ui:initialValue as defaults
    • These were added as optional trailing parameters of the SchemaUtilsType interface's version of getDefaultFormState() as well
  • getDefaultFormState(): Under nestedDefaultsPrecedence: 'ancestorWins', an ancestor's default wins only where the property's types can hold it, falsy or not. An ancestor's 0, false, '', or a null the property's type allows, wins over the property's own default, where the property's default won, and an ancestor's value of a type the property can't hold gives way to the property's default: default: { v: 5 } over v: { type: 'string', default: 'x' } gave { v: 5 } and gives { v: 'x' } (#5624).
  • getDefaultFormState(): Drops object form data a schema whose types leave out object holds, such as { type: 'string' } or { type: 'array' }, and matches object data at every depth, leaving out a property whose data doesn't match. Object data is a plain object with no primitive value of its own, so a Date, or an object whose valueOf() gives an epoch, is kept. Such a field takes its defaults, as one the data lacks, except inside the items of array data, which keep it. Inside object data, a select over object constants, or a type: 'string' select whose enum holds objects, whose data is none of its constants takes its default, and with no default its key is left out: { p: { type: 'object', enum: [{ a: 1 }, { a: 2 }] } } with { p: { a: 3 } } gave { p: { a: 3 } } and gives {}. Add the value to the options to keep it, or give the select a default to replace it (#5522).
  • getDefaultFormState(): Once the form has generated its defaults (initialDefaultsGenerated), the object data of an untyped field is kept as it stands, so the field's own object default no longer fills in the keys its data lacks: { default: { a: 1 } } with { b: 2 } gave { a: 1, b: 2 } and gives { b: 2 }, as a type: 'object' field with that default already did. Give the field type: 'object' and declare the keys as properties with defaults of their own if they should be filled in (#5523).
  • getDisplayLabel(): An object or array schema whose enum or anyOf/oneOf is a non-empty list of constants now displays its label, since it renders as one select for the whole value rather than as the fields of its contents
  • getOptionMatchingSimpleDiscriminator(): Removed. It read the discriminator property only from an option's own properties, so for the options [{ $ref: '#/definitions/A' }, { $ref: '#/definitions/B' }] whose kind is const 'a' and 'b', the data { kind: 'b' } and the discriminator kind it returned undefined. Call getFirstMatchingOption() or getClosestMatchingOption() with the discriminatorField, which read it through the option's $ref, its allOf entries and the rest of its scope, and return 1 there.
  • getPropertySchema(): Reads properties by own key, so a property named like an Object.prototype member that the schema doesn't declare, such as toString or constructor, returns {} rather than the inherited function (#5561)
  • getRenderedOptionSchema(): The option of an object parent is marked with a Symbol flag, beside the required list and type it already took, so its own field offers no extra key beside the parent's even where the form reads an absent additionalProperties as taking any key
  • getSchemaType(): A schema without a type whose const is falsy (0, false, '' or null) now reports the constant's type instead of undefined. See A typeless oneOf/anyOf of constants now renders as a select for what this changes. A type list of three or more entries that starts with null, such as ['null', 'string', 'number'], now resolves to its first type other than null rather than to null, as a two-entry nullable list already did, so it renders that type's field rather than NullField and getDefaultFormState() fills it in as that type: a required list whose first type other than null is boolean starts at false, and one whose first is object or array gets that type's computed defaults. Of the types any list names, it prefers one JSON Schema defines, so a ['null', 'foo', 'string'] resolves to string, and a ['foo', 'string'] to string rather than foo. Its return type narrows from string | string[] | undefined to string | undefined, since it never returned an array, so a caller's Array.isArray() check on it can go (#5331)
  • isRootSchema(): Removed. It compared a schema's content with the root schema's, which is what made shouldRenderOptionalField() mistake a nested field for the root. Compare the field's fieldPath with ROOT_FIELD_PATH instead: fieldPath === ROOT_FIELD_PATH
  • isSelect(): Reads anyOf before oneOf, the same as optionsList(), so a schema carrying both keywords is judged by the list that renders (#5309). sanitizeDataForNewSchema() and findFieldInSchema() read anyOf first too, and omitExtraData() checks the oneOf/anyOf list it prunes by rather than asking isSelect() about the parent
  • optionsList(): Returns undefined instead of throwing when the anyOf/oneOf it reads is not made of constants and no selector field names where the values are. An option with no title of its own and an object or array value is labelled with its JSON instead of [object Object]. A selector property is read by own key, so an option that doesn't declare one named like an Object.prototype member, such as toString, is read by its constant rather than through the inherited function (#5561)
  • orderProperties(): Matches property names by own key. A property named __proto__, declared or held under additionalProperties, is placed at a ui:order wildcard, where it was left out, and a ui:order without a wildcard that doesn't list it now throws, where the property was silently hidden. ObjectField renders that throw as its InvalidObjectField error in place of the object, so add __proto__ or * to such an order. A name like toString that the order lists but the properties don't is dropped rather than returned (#5561)
  • relaxOptionsForScoring(): Removed. omitExtraData() relaxes the whole scope of an option itself, from where the option sits in the root. To score options with their additionalProperties: false relaxed yourself, hand getClosestMatchingOption() or getFirstMatchingOption() copies of them with additionalProperties: true.
  • retrieveSchema(): The stub it builds for a property described only by an additionalProperties with no type now keeps the rest of that subschema instead of discarding it, so a property constrained by an enum, a format, a length or a range renders as a field that honors it rather than as free text. Subschema keywords such as allOf, and a default of another type than the data, are left out, as are the identifiers ($id, $anchor, ...) and containers ($defs, definitions) of a stub whose type the subschema only implies or the data supplies: such a stub is the form's own reading of what one property holds, and copying an $id onto every sibling property would route them all to a field registered under it. This is not gated behind useFallbackUiForUnsupportedType, so such a property renders as the field its constraint calls for in every form, and a value of another type than that constraint allows is as invisible in it as in any field for a schema that names a type. The stub still takes the type of the data the property holds, and is now marked with the new GUESSED_TYPE_FLAG symbol to record that the type was guessed rather than declared by the schema when the subschema asserts nothing about the value. A key whose matching patternProperties subschema names no type is stubbed that way too, where it used to be stubbed with that subschema itself and render as the unsupported field no type can draw. A key that matches none of an object's patternProperties patterns is stubbed from its data the same way, since a schema naming no additionalProperties allows that key as much as additionalProperties: true does; only a schema that forbids such a key still stubs it as { type: 'null' }: an additionalProperties: false, an unevaluatedProperties: false where no additionalProperties evaluates the key, or a matching pattern of false, which rejects every value the key could hold. Which schema describes a key is getAdditionalPropertySchema()'s answer and the type it says the property holds is getAdditionalPropertyType()'s, both of which ObjectField reads to seed a new property, so the field a key renders with and the value it is seeded with cannot disagree. That subschema is resolved before the stub is built, through one ladder for every keyword that can describe a key: an additionalProperties carrying a $ref used to be resolved from that $ref alone, discarding the keywords beside it, where those keywords are now layered over the referenced ones as they are wherever else a $ref appears, and an allOf naming a type now names the stub's type instead of leaving it to the data. A subschema offering an anyOf/oneOf of options that disagree about the type is stubbed without a type of its own, where it used to be stubbed as an object, which rendered an empty object fieldset beside the option selector and seeded the {} no primitive option accepts; options that agree on a type, object included, still name it (#5330). When expanding every branch, resolveAnyOrOneOfSchemas() keeps the keyword it didn't read on each option it returns, so the schema parser also covers the oneOf of a schema whose anyOf it resolved first, which a precompiled validator otherwise threw for at runtime
  • sanitizeDataForNewSchema(): A property is no longer treated as having changed schema when its type differs but both the old and the new type carry GUESSED_TYPE_FLAG, since those types describe the data rather than anything either schema requires. Without this, switching the type of such a property through the fallback UI discarded the value as data belonging to an old schema. A new schema that declares a type of its own is still the type the data has to satisfy. It also compares a default or const with the form data by value rather than by reference, so a readOnly object or array holding its default keeps it, and an untouched object default is swapped for the new schema's. An array item picked from object constants is kept when the new items schema still offers it, rather than sanitized property by property and dropped. An anyOf/oneOf with an option that is neither a const nor an enum no longer counts as a list of allowed values, so a value only that option accepts is kept rather than replaced with one of the constants. An option's enum counts every one of its values as allowed, where one with more than one value used to add none, so a value it allows is kept and one no option allows is cleared. Array items are no longer filtered against the items enum on every pass: with the previous form data passed (the way Form calls it), the filter is skipped when the old and new items schemas, each resolved against its own data, agree - so editing an unrelated field no longer silently drops values the schema offered when they were entered (#5451). Without previous data the filter always runs, matching v6. The filter always runs for a select over object or array constants and for a property the new schema introduces, and a scalar property outside the new enum follows the same agreement rule when previous data is available. Whether a schema or a property is an array is read through getSchemaType(), and two type lists are compared by what they list rather than as objects, so an array whose type list also allows null, such as ['array', 'null'], keeps and sanitizes its items as a plain type: 'array' does, and a property whose type list two options each declare keeps its value across a switch. A tuple, an array declaring no items or the same boolean items, that both schemas describe alike is kept up to the new schema's maxItems rather than cleared, an array the new schema's const rejects is cleared so that the const can take its place, and a property or an array's items whose type list names object, such as ['object', 'null'], is sanitized property by property when it holds an object, as a type: 'object' one is, keeping a null it allows (#5359). A value it sets, clears or sanitizes under a property named __proto__ is written as an own key, where it was lost (#5561)
  • schemaHasNestedConditional(): Removed. Form no longer compares root-level retrieved schemas to decide whether to sanitize: it compares the field trees before and after a change, which reach a dependencies or if at any depth (see Sanitize is a diff of the field trees). Nothing replaces it
  • setByPath(): A __proto__ segment, in any position, is written as an own key through setOwn(), where the path used to be refused and the write dropped. The write itself never reaches the prototype setter, but code of your own that builds the path from user input, such as a key the user typed or a dotted path from a URL, and then copies the result with Object.assign(), a target[key] = source[key] loop or a hand-written recursive merge does reach it, changing the copy's prototype or, through a recursive merge, Object.prototype itself. Copy such a result with spread or setOwn(), or leave __proto__ out of the path. Under additionalProperties: false, AJV doesn't count a declared __proto__ property among the declared ones, so a value written to it fails validation as an additional property (#5561)
  • shouldRenderOptionalField(): Takes the field's fieldPath as a required fifth argument, and its fourth, uiSchema, is no longer optional: shouldRenderOptionalField(registry, schema, required, uiSchema, fieldPath). A field of your own passes the fieldPath from its props; a JavaScript caller that still passes four arguments gets no error, and its root field renders behind an Add button, since a missing fieldPath is not the root's. It returns false for the root field, and no longer mistakes a nested field for it: the option a root anyOf/oneOf selects no longer gets the controls, while a nested object or array that a recursive $ref: '#' describes now does
  • toErrorSchema() and ErrorSchemaBuilder: Write through setByPath(), so an error at a path through a __proto__ key is filed under that key as an own key, where it was dropped. An error a transformErrors points at .__proto__ reaches that field, since the validators build their errorSchema with toErrorSchema() after it runs (#5561)

    • A layout grid row without a column template lays out on 12 tracks in chakra-ui, fluentui-rc and shadcn BREAKING CHANGE
    • A custom GridTemplate is handed a fieldId BREAKING CHANGE
    • Field identity is a FieldPath string instead of a FieldPathId object BREAKING CHANGE
    • Ids can't collide or split an id list BREAKING CHANGE
    • IChangeEvent members are read-only BREAKING CHANGE
    • IChangeEvent has required dirty, dirtyFields, touched, touchedFields and submitCount, and FormRef a required getStatus() BREAKING CHANGE
    • ui:emptyValue extended scope BREAKING CHANGE
    • Shallow comparison replaces experimental_componentUpdateStrategy BREAKING CHANGE
    • A type list follows its ui:widget to the field and class it renders BREAKING CHANGE
    • A typeless oneOf/anyOf of constants now renders as a select BREAKING CHANGE
    • A boolean enum labels its values Yes/No BREAKING CHANGE
    • ui:enumOrder orders constant anyOf/oneOf options BREAKING CHANGE
    • EnumValue includes null, objects and arrays BREAKING CHANGE
    • number/integer fields no longer render a native <input type="number"> by default BREAKING CHANGE
    • A BaseInputTemplate of your own forwards inputMode and pattern BREAKING CHANGE
    • FieldTemplateProps gains a required keyName BREAKING CHANGE
    • ui:hideError now suppresses the theme's error styling BREAKING CHANGE
    • A discriminated cell of a layout grid renders through SchemaField BREAKING CHANGE
    • A LayoutGridField with no layout, or a cell or condition naming no field, renders nothing BREAKING CHANGE
    • A layout grid cell is named by its property name, not its dotted path BREAKING CHANGE
    • EnumOptionsType.value is unknown BREAKING CHANGE
    • AnyOfField and OneOfField take their options already retrieved BREAKING CHANGE
    • FieldTemplateProps.rawHelp carries an element ui:help BREAKING CHANGE
    • Clearing a custom error now also clears it from the error list BREAKING CHANGE
    • An error a field raises is kept apart from the validator's BREAKING CHANGE
    • The errorSchema passed to onChange holds only the field's own errors BREAKING CHANGE
    • A custom ArraySchemaField is handed each item's own errors as rawErrors BREAKING CHANGE
    • noValidate now turns off live validation on blur BREAKING CHANGE
    • FormRef.validate() takes only the data BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/daisyui applies ui:classNames and ui:style on the field wrapper BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/mantine widgets reference rjsf's ids for labels and descriptions BREAKING CHANGE
    • getDisplayLabel() reads a boolean's widget from the reduced ui options BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/daisyui's date and label markup changed BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/daisyui's useTheme() reads the stored theme, and ThemeContext is removed BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/daisyui no longer ships src/styles.css or depends on tailwindcss BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/daisyui's SelectWidget names its open list of options by the field's label BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/shadcn's SelectWidget names its combobox and fills empty placeholders BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/shadcn's multiple SelectWidget takes its field's id and opens only on user action BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/shadcn's SelectWidget names its list of options by the field's label BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/shadcn's RangeWidget ignores name, disabled, value and defaultValue from ui:options.props BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/mantine ignores id, name, value, defaultValue, readOnly, autoFocus, data, multiple, error, onChange, onBlur and onFocus in ui:options BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/mui's widgets keep the form's value, disabled state and handlers over ui:options.mui BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/mui's descriptions render a div rather than an <h6> BREAKING CHANGE
    • An object's or an array's group has role="group" and the field's id BREAKING CHANGE
    • AltDateWidget date parts are named in every theme BREAKING CHANGE
    • AltDateWidget hands an unset date part on as undefined, and useAltDateWidgetProps() returns buttonsDisabled BREAKING CHANGE
    • enumOptionValueEncoder() is removed in favor of enumOptionsDomValues() BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/utils schema functions take a SchemaContext in place of the validator BREAKING CHANGE
    • findSelectedOptionInXxxOf() returns the closest option for options with no discriminator BREAKING CHANGE
    • A LayoutGridField cell naming a property beside anyOf/oneOf, or of options with no discriminator, renders the field BREAKING CHANGE
    • A LayoutGridField cell naming a property of discriminated options beside the grid renders nothing BREAKING CHANGE
    • A property declared beside anyOf/oneOf and in an option is read from beside them BREAKING CHANGE
    • A custom ObjectFieldTemplate asks registry.schemaUtils.canExpand() BREAKING CHANGE
    • An $id under an unknown keyword, such as components or x-*, names no schema BREAKING CHANGE
    • localToUTC() can return null BREAKING CHANGE
    • A non-object field's anyOf/oneOf option renders with its parent's keywords BREAKING CHANGE
    • An option selector stays a select for a text, updown or range ui:widget its options inherit BREAKING CHANGE
    • An anyOf/oneOf option naming no type takes its field's type for the Optional Data Controls BREAKING CHANGE
    • An empty object counts as added data for the Optional Data Controls BREAKING CHANGE
    • A field's label, description, help and errors are drawn where its plan says BREAKING CHANGE
    • Breaking changes: schema resolution
    • Option selection and cycle expansion are form state
    • Sanitize is a diff of the field trees BREAKING CHANGE
    • A field is named once per data path BREAKING CHANGE
    • getUiOptions() returns a field's options alone BREAKING CHANGE
    • ui:options ignores field and the other keys it doesn't take BREAKING CHANGE
    • A custom field rendering FallbackField without a plan has the value field draw its label BREAKING CHANGE
    • ui:globalOptions hold only the options RJSF reads there BREAKING CHANGE
    • A forbidden extra key says so on its row BREAKING CHANGE
    • A dependency anyOf, or a dependency oneOf whose options don't declare the dependency's key, now applies BREAKING CHANGE
    • GridType, Operators and TranslatableString are as const objects BREAKING CHANGE
    • mergeObjects() and mergeSchemas() require an object first argument BREAKING CHANGE
    • The root field never renders the Optional Data Controls BREAKING CHANGE
    • An additionalProperties entry never renders the Optional Data Controls BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/antd's colSpan is keyed by the widget a property renders BREAKING CHANGE
    • @rjsf/antd and @rjsf/mantine leave out a property hidden by deprecatedHandling or ui:definitions BREAKING CHANGE
    • A $ref cycle whose field renders hidden has no Expand button BREAKING CHANGE
    • An array item's handlers do only what its buttons can BREAKING CHANGE
    • Copy shows only from a tuple's last fixed item on BREAKING CHANGE
    • A disabled or read-only array item disables its own buttons BREAKING CHANGE
    • sanitizeDataForNewSchema() removes the keys it discards, and leaves out objects the data doesn't hold BREAKING CHANGE
  • New Features
    • getFormData() and the FormRef type
    • transformChange
    • ui:initialValue and ui:required
    • ui:options.optgroups for grouped <select> options
    • propertyNames.enum renders the key as a dropdown
    • Multiple types and unconstrained properties can be edited through the fallback UI
    • additionalPropertiesWhenAbsent reads an object naming no additionalProperties as the spec does
    • Utilities no other RJSF package uses are no longer exported from @rjsf/utils BREAKING CHANGE
    • New types
    • Type-safe UiSchema (opt-in)
    • New utility React components
    • New utility functions
    • Changes to existing utility functions
